key text: The Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017 are made by the Central Government under Section 118 of the MV Act. They replaced the Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: The Driving Regulations 2017 replaced the old Rules of the Road Regulations, 1989.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Breaking any driving regulation is punished under Section 177A: ₹500 for the first offence and ₹1,500 for later offences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Keep left: a driver must drive as close to the left side of the road as is safe, and let oncoming traffic pass on the right.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: On a one-way road, the driver must not drive against the direction of traffic. Reversing into a one-way road is also not allowed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turning left: keep close to the left edge before and after the turn.
recall answer: Close to the left side of the road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turning right: move close to the centre of the road (on a two-way road) before turning, and after turning keep to the left of the new road.
recall answer: Near the centre line of the road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Give the correct indicator signal before turning, changing lane, stopping or pulling out, early enough for others to see.
recall answer: Well before, in time for others to react.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lane driving: on a road with lanes, drive inside one lane and change lanes only after signalling and checking it is safe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: On multi-lane roads, slow vehicles use the left lane. The right lane is mainly for overtaking and faster traffic.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overtaking is normally done from the right side of the vehicle in front.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: You may overtake from the left only when the vehicle ahead has signalled a right turn and moved towards the centre.
recall answer: When the vehicle ahead has signalled and moved to turn right.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not overtake: at bends, hill tops, junctions and pedestrian crossings; when the road ahead is not clearly visible; or where a solid line or sign forbids it.
recall answer: Bends, hill tops, junctions, pedestrian crossings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not overtake if the vehicle behind you has already started to overtake you.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: When being overtaken, do not speed up. Keep left and slow a little if needed so the other driver can pass quickly.
recall answer: Keep left and do not increase speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: When overtaking a cyclist, pedestrian or animal, leave enough side gap and pass slowly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: At a junction without signals or signs, give way to traffic coming from your right.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: When entering a main road from a side road, give way to the traffic on the main road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: At a roundabout, give way to traffic already in the roundabout (coming from your right).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: At a zebra crossing, stop and give way to pedestrians who are crossing or waiting to cross.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Give free passage to emergency vehicles like ambulances and fire engines by moving to the left and stopping if needed.
recall answer: Move to the left and give way.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Not giving way to emergency vehicles is an offence under Section 194E: ₹10,000 fine, imprisonment up to 6 months, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: On narrow hill roads, the vehicle going downhill should give way to the vehicle going uphill.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never drive faster than the speed limit, and drive slower when the road, weather, traffic or light is poor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Speed limits are fixed under Section 112. Overspeeding is punished under Section 183: ₹1,000–2,000 for light vehicles and ₹2,000–4,000 for medium and heavy vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Keep a safe gap from the vehicle in front, enough to stop if it brakes suddenly. A simple guide is the two-second rule, doubled in rain.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Use the horn only when needed to warn. Do not sound it continuously, needlessly or in silence zones near hospitals, schools and courts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Multi-tone, pressure and unusually loud horns are not allowed. Using a horn in a silence zone is punished under Section 194F.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dip the headlights when meeting oncoming traffic, when following another vehicle closely, and on well-lit city roads.
recall answer: Meeting oncoming traffic or following another vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Use hazard warning lights when your vehicle has broken down or stopped in an emergency on the road. Do not use them while driving normally.
recall answer: When stopped in an emergency or broken down.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Use fog lamps only in fog or poor visibility, along with low beam. High beam in fog reflects back and blinds you.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand signal for stop: raise the right forearm vertically outside the vehicle, palm facing forward.
recall answer: Right forearm raised vertically, palm forward.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand signal for slowing down: extend the right arm with palm down and move it up and down several times.
recall answer: Right arm out, palm down, moved up and down.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand signal for turning right: extend the right arm straight out horizontally, palm facing forward.
recall answer: Right arm straight out, palm forward.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand signal for turning left: extend the right arm and rotate it anticlockwise.
recall answer: Right arm extended and rotated anticlockwise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand signal to let the vehicle behind overtake: extend the right arm below shoulder level and swing it backward and forward.
recall answer: Right arm below shoulder, swung back and forth.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not park at or near a junction, bend, hill top, bridge, pedestrian crossing, traffic light, bus stop or school and hospital entrance.
recall answer: Junction, bend, bridge, pedestrian crossing, bus stop.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not park on a footpath, cycle track, on the wrong side, opposite another parked vehicle on a narrow road, near a fire hydrant, or where the kerb is painted yellow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Park on the left, parallel to the kerb unless marked otherwise. Switch off the engine, apply the parking brake and lock the vehicle.
recall answer: Switch off engine; apply parking brake.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not open a door without checking traffic. Open it slowly and get out on the footpath side where possible.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reverse only as much as needed, slowly, after checking behind. Do not reverse from a side road into a main road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not take a U-turn where it is prohibited, on busy roads or where you cannot see far in both directions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not enter a yellow box junction unless your exit is clear. Stop behind the stop line at signals.
recall answer: Only when your exit is clear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not drive in a lane reserved for buses or other vehicles, and never drive on a footpath or cycle track.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Towing: use a tow bar, rope or chain clearly visible to others, tow only one vehicle, and drive slowly (about 25 km/h).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not use a hand-held mobile phone while driving. Hands-free use for navigation is allowed if it does not distract.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand-held phone use while driving is treated as dangerous driving under Section 184: ₹1,000–5,000 for the first offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driver and all passengers must wear seat belts. Two-wheeler riders and pillions above 4 years must wear helmets.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Children aged 9 months to 4 years on a two-wheeler need a crash helmet and a safety harness, and the speed must not exceed 40 km/h.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: A two-wheeler may carry only one pillion rider, seated on a proper seat behind the driver (Section 128).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: At an unguarded railway level crossing, stop the vehicle, and the conductor or driver must walk to the crossing and check no train is coming (Section 131).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never drive after drinking alcohol. The legal limit is 30 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood (Section 185).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not cut into or break through a funeral procession, military convoy or police procession.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not stop or park on the carriageway of a highway except in an emergency. A broken-down vehicle must show hazard lights and a warning triangle placed well behind.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: On roads divided by a median, never drive on the right half. Cross the median only at openings provided.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not carry a load that sticks out dangerously, blocks the driver's view, or is not tied securely.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving on the wrong side, jumping red lights and driving in the wrong direction on a one-way road are punished as dangerous driving (Section 184).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: the regulations say 'give way to traffic from the right' at uncontrolled junctions, but at roundabouts this also means traffic already in the circle.
recall answer: Traffic on your right (already in the roundabout).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor Vehicles (Driving) Regulations, 2017; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chapter II of the MV Act (Sections 3 to 28) deals with licensing of drivers of motor vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 3: no person shall drive a motor vehicle in a public place without an effective driving licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 3 also says a medium or heavy transport vehicle (bus, lorry) can be driven only if the licence specially allows it.
recall answer: No; the licence must cover that transport vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A learner can drive under Section 3 if they hold a learner's licence and follow its conditions, such as having an instructor and L plate.
recall answer: A learner's licence holder under its conditions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 4: minimum age to drive a motor vehicle in a public place is 18 years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A person of 16 years can drive a motorcycle with engine up to 50 cc, after the age of 16, with consent of a parent or guardian.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 4: a transport vehicle can be driven only after the age of 20 years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 5: an owner must not let a person drive their vehicle unless that person has a valid licence and meets the age rules.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Penalty for owner allowing an unauthorised person to drive is under Section 180: up to ₹5,000, imprisonment up to 3 months, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving without a licence or under age (against Sections 3 or 4) is punished under Section 181: up to ₹5,000, imprisonment up to 3 months, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 6: a person shall not hold more than one driving licence, and cannot get one while disqualified.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 6 also says a licence holder must not let anyone else use their licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 7 restricts learner's licences for certain vehicles. A 16-year-old can get a learner's licence only for a motorcycle up to 50 cc, with guardian consent.
recall answer: Motorcycle up to 50 cc, with guardian's consent.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 8: the licensing authority grants a learner's licence after the applicant passes a test on traffic rules, signs and duties.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: An applicant can apply for a learner's licence to any licensing authority in the State where they live or work.
recall answer: Any licensing authority in the State where you live or work.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Medical certificate (Form 1A, by a registered doctor) is needed for a transport vehicle licence and for applicants above 40 years. Others give a self-declaration of fitness.
recall answer: Transport vehicle applicants and those above 40.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A learner's licence is valid for 6 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A learner can take the driving test only after 30 days from the date the learner's licence was issued, and within its 6-month validity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A learner must show an 'L' plate (red L on white) on the front and back of the vehicle.
recall answer: L plate: red L on white background.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: A learner driving a car must have an instructor with a valid licence sitting beside them. A learner on a motorcycle may carry only an instructor as pillion.
recall answer: A person holding a valid DL for that vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 9: a driving licence is granted after the applicant passes a test of competence to drive (driving test).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Those who pass from an accredited driver training centre can be exempted from the driving test at the RTO (2019 amendment).
recall answer: Those certified by an accredited driver training centre.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Traditional Kerala test: 'H' track for four-wheelers and figure '8' track for two-wheelers, followed by a road test. Kerala revised the test pattern in 2024.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 10 gives the form and contents of licences and the classes of vehicles a licence can cover.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Classes under Section 10(2): motorcycle without gear, motorcycle with gear, invalid carriage, light motor vehicle, transport vehicle, e-cart or e-rickshaw, road roller, and vehicle of a specified description.
recall answer: MCWOG, MCWG, LMV, transport vehicle (also invalid carriage, e-rickshaw, road roller).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: The e-cart and e-rickshaw class was added by the 2015 amendment.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: LMV (light motor vehicle) is a vehicle with gross vehicle weight up to 7,500 kg. Cars, jeeps and small goods vehicles fall in this class.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Supreme Court (Mukund Dewangan case, 2017; upheld 2024): an LMV licence holder can drive a transport vehicle of LMV class (GVW up to 7,500 kg) without separate endorsement.
recall answer: Yes, as per Supreme Court (Mukund Dewangan).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 11: a licence holder can apply to add another class of vehicle to their licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 12: licensing and regulation of driving schools. The 2019 amendment added accredited driver training centres.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 13: a learner's licence or driving licence issued in any State is valid throughout India.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 14 gives the validity (currency) of licences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transport vehicle licence is valid for 5 years (2019). For vehicles carrying hazardous goods it is valid for 3 years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Non-transport licence validity: if taken before 30 years of age, valid till the holder turns 40.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Non-transport licence taken between 30 and 50 years is valid for 10 years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Non-transport licence taken between 50 and 55 is valid till the holder turns 60. Taken after 55, it is valid for 5 years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: validity of a non-transport DL
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 15 deals with renewal of driving licences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: You can apply for renewal up to one year before expiry or within one year after expiry. After one year from expiry, a fresh driving test is needed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 16: the licensing authority can revoke a licence if the holder has a disease or disability that makes driving dangerous.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 17: an order refusing or revoking a licence must give reasons. The person can appeal against it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 18: licences to drive motor vehicles belonging to the Central Government, such as defence vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 19: the licensing authority can disqualify a person from holding a licence or revoke it, after giving them a chance to be heard.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Grounds under Section 19: habitual criminal or drunkard, drug addict, using the vehicle for a crime, dangerous driving record, licence obtained by fraud, or refusing a test.
recall answer: Habitual drunkard, licence by fraud, vehicle used for crime.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 19(1A) (2019): for offences like overspeeding, dangerous driving, drunk driving, overloading and not wearing seat belt or helmet, the licence can be suspended for at least 3 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: The authority may also order the driver to complete a driver refresher training course before getting the licence back.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 20 lets a court disqualify a person from holding a licence when convicting them of certain offences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 22: suspension or cancellation of a licence on conviction for certain offences, such as causing death or grievous hurt with a vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 23: a disqualified person cannot hold or get a licence during the period of disqualification. Their licence has no effect.
recall answer: Licence is ineffective; no new licence during the period.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving while disqualified is punished under Section 182: ₹10,000 fine, imprisonment up to 3 months, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 24: endorsement. The court or authority records the conviction or disqualification on the driving licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 25: endorsements move to any new licence. After a set period without further offences, a clean licence can be issued.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 25A (2019): National Register of Driving Licences. All State registers feed into it; it runs on the Sarathi system.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sarathi is the online system for licences; Vahan is the online system for vehicle registration.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 27: power of the Central Government to make rules on licensing (tests, forms, fees, medical standards).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 28: power of the State Government to make rules for Chapter II, like licensing authorities and appeals.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Licensing authority is the officer authorised by the State to issue licences, usually the RTO or Joint RTO.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving licence can be held in electronic form (DigiLocker or mParivahan). A smart card DL is also issued.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: An International Driving Permit (IDP) is issued by the licensing authority to Indian licence holders for driving abroad. It is valid for one year.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Juvenile offence (Section 199A): if a minor drives, the guardian or owner is guilty: ₹25,000 fine and up to 3 years' imprisonment. The vehicle's RC is cancelled for 12 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 199A, a juvenile who commits a driving offence cannot get a learner's or driving licence until age 25.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: Section 3 is about need for a licence; Section 4 is about age. Section 5 is owner's duty; Section 6 is one licence only.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: Section 8 is learner's licence; Section 9 is driving licence; Section 10 is classes; Section 11 is adding a class.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Licensing of drivers: MV Act sections 3 to 28; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 2 of the MV Act gives the definitions. Exam questions often ask the clause number or the key limit in a definition.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Adapted vehicle, Section 2(1): a vehicle specially designed, or altered under Section 52, for the sole use of a person with a physical defect or disability.
recall answer: Vehicle built or altered for the sole use of a person with disability (Sec 2(1)).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Adapted vehicle can be made by alteration under Section 52, and it must be used only by or for that disabled person.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aggregator, Section 2(1A): a digital intermediary or marketplace that connects a passenger with a driver for transport, like Uber or Ola. Added in 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aggregators need a licence under Section 93 and must follow the guidelines issued by the Central Government.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Articulated vehicle, Section 2(2): a motor vehicle to which a semi-trailer is attached.
recall answer: Motor vehicle with a semi-trailer attached (Sec 2(2)).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gross vehicle weight (GVW), Section 2(15): the total weight of the vehicle and load certified and registered by the registering authority as permissible for that vehicle.
recall answer: Total permissible weight of vehicle + load, certified and registered.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Unladen weight, Section 2(48): weight of the vehicle with all equipment ordinarily used, but without the driver or attendant.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: If alternative bodies or parts are used, unladen weight is taken with the heaviest such body or part.
recall answer: The heaviest alternative body or part.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Light motor vehicle, Section 2(21): transport vehicle or omnibus with GVW, or motor car, tractor or road roller with unladen weight, not exceeding 7,500 kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heavy goods vehicle, Section 2(16): a goods carriage with GVW, or a tractor or road roller with unladen weight, exceeding 12,000 kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heavy passenger motor vehicle, Section 2(17): public or private service vehicle, educational institution bus or omnibus with GVW, or a motor car with unladen weight, exceeding 12,000 kg.
recall answer: GVW (or motor car unladen weight) above 12,000 kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Medium goods vehicle, Section 2(23): any goods carriage that is neither a light motor vehicle nor a heavy goods vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Medium passenger motor vehicle, Section 2(24): a public or private service vehicle or educational institution bus other than a motorcycle, invalid carriage, LMV or HPMV.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Classify a goods vehicle by GVW
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motor cab, Section 2(25): a vehicle made or adapted to carry not more than 6 passengers, excluding the driver, for hire or reward.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Maxi cab, Section 2(22): a vehicle made or adapted to carry more than 6 but not more than 12 passengers, excluding the driver, for hire or reward.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motor car, Section 2(26): any motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle, omnibus, road roller, tractor, motorcycle or invalid carriage.
recall answer: No; it is a transport vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Omnibus, Section 2(29): any motor vehicle made or adapted to carry more than 6 persons, excluding the driver.
recall answer: Vehicle to carry more than 6 persons, excluding driver (Sec 2(29)).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Private service vehicle, Section 2(33): carries more than 6 persons, excluding driver, used by the owner for their trade or business, not for hire or reward.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: A private service vehicle does not include a motor vehicle used for public purposes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Public service vehicle, Section 2(35): any motor vehicle used for carrying passengers for hire or reward. It includes maxi cab, motor cab, contract carriage and stage carriage.
recall answer: Maxi cab, motor cab, contract carriage, stage carriage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stage carriage, Section 2(40): carries more than 6 passengers for hire, charging separate fares per passenger for the whole or stages of a journey.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Contract carriage, Section 2(7): carries passengers for hire under a contract for the whole vehicle, for a fixed or agreed rate, without stopping to pick up others.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transport vehicle, Section 2(47): a public service vehicle, a goods carriage, an educational institution bus or a private service vehicle.
recall answer: Public service vehicle, goods carriage, educational institution bus, private service vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: an educational institution bus and a private service vehicle are transport vehicles even though they are not for hire.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Goods carriage, Section 2(14): a motor vehicle made or adapted only for carrying goods, or any vehicle used for carrying goods.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap with numbers: 2(15) GVW, 2(16) heavy goods, 2(17) heavy passenger, 2(21) LMV, 2(22) maxi cab, 2(25) motor cab, 2(26) motor car, 2(29) omnibus.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: More clause numbers: 2(1) adapted vehicle, 2(1A) aggregator, 2(2) articulated vehicle, 2(33) private service vehicle, 2(35) public service vehicle, 2(47) transport vehicle, 2(48) unladen weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motor vehicle, Section 2(28): any mechanically propelled vehicle adapted for use on roads. It excludes vehicles on fixed rails and special factory vehicles, and vehicles with engine up to 25 cc.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Good Samaritan, Section 2(12A): a person who, in good faith and without expecting reward, gives emergency help at an accident or takes the victim to hospital.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: MV Act Section 2: definitions
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act Section 2: definitions; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 39: no person shall drive, and no owner shall allow, a motor vehicle in a public place unless it is registered and shows its registration mark.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 39 also needs the RC to be valid: not suspended or cancelled.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exception to Section 39: a vehicle in the possession of a dealer, used under a trade certificate.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Using a vehicle without registration is punished under Section 192: first offence ₹2,000 to ₹5,000; later offences up to 1 year jail or ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 fine, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Temporary registration (Section 43) is valid for one month. It lets a new vehicle be driven until permanent registration.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 44: the registering authority may ask the owner to produce the vehicle at the time of registration to check its details.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: After the 2019 amendment, a new non-transport vehicle sold by an authorised dealer can be registered at the dealer's place without producing it before the authority.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 46: a vehicle registered in any State does not need to be registered again in another State. Registration is valid throughout India.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: But under Section 47, if the vehicle is kept in another State for more than 12 months, the owner must apply for a new registration mark there.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 52: no owner shall alter a vehicle so that its details in the RC differ from those originally given by the manufacturer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Allowed alterations under Section 52: change of fuel (like CNG, LPG or electric kits) using approved kits, retro-fitment for adapted vehicles, and others notified by the Central Government.
recall answer: Yes, with an approved kit and RC endorsement.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Replacing the engine with one of the same type is allowed, but the owner must inform the registering authority.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: When an approved alteration is made, the owner must inform the registering authority within 14 days so the RC can be endorsed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Illegal alteration is punished under Section 182A(4) with ₹5,000 for each alteration.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 53: the registering authority can suspend the registration if the vehicle is unsafe to use or does not meet Chapter VII standards.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Registration can also be suspended under Section 53 if a vehicle is used for hire or reward without a valid permit.
recall answer: Unsafe condition; used for hire without permit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: The owner must be given a chance to be heard before suspension, and must surrender the RC when suspended.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 55: cancellation of registration. If a vehicle is destroyed or permanently unusable, the owner must report within 14 days and send the RC to the registering authority.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other grounds for cancellation under Section 55: vehicle permanently taken out of India, registration got by fraud, or chassis or engine details do not match records.
recall answer: Permanently removed from India, fraud, mismatched chassis.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 56: a transport vehicle is not validly registered unless it carries a certificate of fitness.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fitness certificates are issued by the prescribed authority (MVI) or by an authorised or automated testing station.
recall answer: Prescribed authority or authorised (automated) testing station.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: The authority can cancel a fitness certificate if the vehicle no longer meets the rules. The Central Government can extend fitness checks to other classes of vehicles.
recall answer: Yes, if the vehicle becomes unfit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Non-transport vehicle RC is valid for 15 years from issue, then renewable for 5 years at a time (Section 41).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: Section 39 necessity, 44 production, 46 valid all India, 52 alteration, 53 suspension, 55 cancellation, 56 fitness.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Registration: Sections 39 to 56
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Registration: Sections 39 to 56; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 66: no owner shall use a transport vehicle in a public place except under the conditions of a permit granted or countersigned by an RTA, STA or prescribed authority.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Permit exemptions under Section 66(3) include government vehicles not used commercially, police, ambulances, fire services and funeral vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Another Section 66(3) exemption: goods vehicles with GVW not exceeding 3,000 kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Battery-operated transport vehicles (and those running on ethanol or methanol) are exempted from permit requirement by central notification.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Using a vehicle without a permit is punished under Section 192A: up to ₹10,000 fine and up to 6 months' imprisonment for the first offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of permits: stage carriage, contract carriage, private service vehicle, goods carriage, temporary, national, tourist and special permits.
recall answer: Stage carriage, contract carriage, goods carriage, tourist.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: A temporary permit (Section 87) is for a short need, like a festival or season. It is valid for up to 4 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Regular permits are generally valid for 5 years (Section 81).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: A State Transport Undertaking (STU) is a government-run transport service. KSRTC is Kerala's STU.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Chapter VI of the MV Act has special provisions for State Transport Undertakings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 99: if the State thinks it is in the public interest, it may prepare a proposal for road transport services to be run by an STU, fully or partly excluding private operators.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: The Section 99 proposal must give the nature of services and the area or route. It is published in the Official Gazette and in at least one regional-language newspaper.
recall answer: Official Gazette and at least one regional-language newspaper.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Objections to the proposal can be filed within 30 days of publication (Section 100). The scheme must be approved within one year, or the proposal lapses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: When an approved scheme excludes private operators from a route, it is called a nationalised route. Private permits are not granted there.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Purpose words in Section 99: 'efficient, adequate, economical and properly coordinated road transport service'.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99)
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Permits (Sec 66) and STU schemes (Sec 99); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 109: every motor vehicle must be built and maintained so that the driver has effective control of it at all times.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 109 also says vehicles must have right-hand steering, unless fitted with a proper mechanical or electrical signalling device.
recall answer: A mechanical or electrical signalling device.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 109, the Central Government can notify standards for vehicles and components, such as AIS and BIS standards, for safety.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 110: the Central Government makes rules on construction, equipment and maintenance (lights, brakes, tyres, emissions, and more). These are in CMVR.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 110A (2019): the Central Government can order a manufacturer to recall vehicles of a type or variant that have a defect harmful to the environment, driver, passengers or other road users.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: A recall can follow complaints from a set percentage of owners, a testing agency's report, or other sources.
recall answer: Complaints from a notified percentage of owners, or a testing agency report.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: In a recall, the manufacturer must reimburse buyers the full cost, or replace the vehicle with a similar or better one, or fix it, and may also pay a penalty.
recall answer: Repair, replacement or full refund (and pay penalty).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: A manufacturer who finds a defect itself must inform the Central Government and start a voluntary recall.
recall answer: Yes, voluntary recall after informing the Government.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 110B (2019): every motor vehicle must have a type-approval certificate showing it meets the standards, issued by an authorised testing agency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Testing agencies include ARAI (Pune), ICAT (Manesar), CIRT (Pune), VRDE (Ahmednagar) and NATRAX (Indore).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 110B also allows the Central Government to regulate testing agencies, and to exempt some vehicles, like those for research or export, from type approval.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Selling vehicles that break Chapter VII standards is punished under Section 182A(1): up to 1 year jail or fine up to ₹100 crore, or both, for manufacturers, importers or dealers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 182A(2), makers of unsafe components can be fined up to ₹1 crore or jailed up to 1 year, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 182B punishes contravention of Section 62A, which deals with over-dimensioned vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: 109 general construction, 110 central rules, 110A recall, 110B type approval. Recall and type approval were both added in 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B)
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Construction, recall and type approval (Sec 109, 110A, 110B); standard diploma textbook

key text: Chapter VIII of the MV Act deals with control of traffic (Sections 112 to 138).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 112: no one shall drive a vehicle faster than the maximum speed, or slower than the minimum speed, fixed for it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 112, the State Government or an authorised authority can set lower speed limits for certain areas or roads, by notification and road signs. They cannot exceed the central maximum.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 112 speed limits do not apply to fire, ambulance and police vehicles used on duty when needed.
recall answer: No, it is exempted when needed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 113: limits of weight and limits on use. No one shall drive a vehicle whose laden weight is more than the GVW in its RC, or whose axle load is more than allowed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 113, the State can also make conditions on the use of transport vehicles, such as banning heavy vehicles on certain roads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 114: an authorised MVD officer who suspects overloading can make the driver take the vehicle to a weighing device within 10 km.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: If the vehicle is overloaded, the officer can order the extra load to be unloaded at the owner's risk before it moves on.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overloading is punished under Section 194: ₹20,000 plus ₹2,000 per extra tonne, and the cost of offloading.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Refusing to stop for weighing, or removing load before weighing, is punished under Section 194(2) with ₹40,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 120: a vehicle with left-hand steering must not be driven unless it has a working mechanical or electrical signalling device.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 122: no person in charge shall leave a vehicle or trailer in a public place in a position that causes danger, obstruction or inconvenience to others.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Obstructing traffic flow by a parked or left vehicle is punished under Section 201: ₹500 per hour, plus towing charges.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 123: no driver shall carry people on the running board, roof or bonnet, and no person shall travel there.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 123 binds both the driver (must not allow) and the passenger (must not travel).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 125: a driver shall not allow any person to stand or sit, or anything to be placed, in a way that hampers control of the vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 126: a vehicle must not be left stationary in a public place unless a licensed driver is in the seat, or the engine is stopped and brakes applied so it cannot move.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 127: a vehicle left unattended in a public place for 10 hours or more, or parked where banned, can be towed or clamped on a uniformed police officer's order.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 127, wrecked, burnt or dismantled vehicles causing a hazard can be removed to a police station or authorised place. The owner pays the towing and storage costs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 128: a two-wheeler driver shall not carry more than one person besides themselves, and the pillion must sit on a proper seat fixed behind the driver.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 128 lets the Central Government prescribe safety measures like hand grips, footrests and saree guards for pillion riders.
recall answer: Hand grip, footrest or saree guard.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Breaking Section 128 is punished under Section 194C: ₹1,000 and licence disqualification for 3 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 129: every person driving or riding a motorcycle in a public place must wear protective headgear (helmet) meeting BIS standards.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exemption under Section 129: a Sikh person wearing a turban.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Protective headgear means a helmet that gives protection by its shape, material and build, and is fastened securely to the head by straps.
recall answer: Protective shape/material and securely fastened with straps.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 129 (2019) applies to all persons above 4 years, and the Centre can make safety rules for children below 4 on motorcycles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Not wearing a helmet is punished under Section 194D: ₹1,000 and licence disqualification for 3 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 131: at an unguarded railway level crossing, the driver must stop. The conductor, cleaner or another person must walk to the crossing to check both sides for trains.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: If there is no one else in the vehicle, the driver must get down and check for trains before crossing (Section 131).
recall answer: The driver gets down and checks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 132: the driver must stop and stay when asked by a police officer not below Sub-Inspector in uniform, if the vehicle was in an accident.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 132 also says the driver must stop if a person in charge of an animal asks, fearing the animal may become unmanageable.
recall answer: Yes, if the animal may become unmanageable.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 132, the driver must give their name and address and the owner's name and address when asked.
recall answer: Own name and address, and owner's name and address.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 133: the owner must give, when an authorised police officer asks, the name, address and licence details of the driver or conductor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 134: after an accident with injury, the driver must take reasonable steps to get medical help for the injured, by taking them to the nearest doctor or hospital.
recall answer: Get medical help for the injured (Sec 134).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exception in Section 134: the driver need not do this if it is not possible due to mob fury or other reasons beyond control.
recall answer: Mob fury or reasons beyond control.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 134, the doctor or hospital must treat the injured at once, without waiting for procedural formalities.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 134, the driver must report the accident at the nearest police station as soon as possible, and within 24 hours.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 134, the driver must give the insurer in writing: policy number and validity, date, time and place of accident, details of persons hurt or killed, and driver and licence details.
recall answer: Policy number, date/time/place, injured persons, driver and DL details.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Failing in duties under Sections 132, 133 or 134 is punished under Section 187: up to 6 months or ₹5,000, or both; later offences up to 1 year or ₹10,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 134A: a Good Samaritan is not liable in any civil or criminal action for injury or death of the victim caused by their negligence while helping.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Good Samaritan rules: a helper cannot be forced to give their name or be a witness, and cannot be detained at the hospital or asked to pay.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 136: after an accident, a person authorised by the State (usually an MVI) can inspect the vehicle, enter premises where it is kept, and remove it for examination.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 136, the owner is told where the vehicle is taken, and it is returned after the inspection formalities.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 136A (2019): the State must ensure electronic monitoring and enforcement of road safety on National and State Highways and city roads as notified.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Devices under Section 136A include speed cameras, CCTV, speed guns, body-worn cameras, dashboard cameras and ANPR (automatic number plate recognition).
recall answer: Speed camera, CCTV, body-worn camera, ANPR.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rule 167A of CMVR gives details of electronic enforcement. Notice of the offence (e-challan) is sent within 15 days.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kerala's 'Safe Kerala' project uses AI cameras across the State for electronic enforcement under Section 136A.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: 112 speed, 113 weight, 114 weighing, 120 left-hand control, 122 dangerous position, 123 running board, 125 obstruction of driver, 126 stationary vehicle, 127 abandoned vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: More numbers: 128 pillion safety, 129 helmet, 131 rail crossing, 132 stop, 133 owner info, 134 accident duty, 134A Good Samaritan, 136 inspection, 136A electronic enforcement.
recall answer: Duty of owner to give information.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Control of traffic: Sections 112 to 136A; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 146: no person shall use, or allow another to use, a motor vehicle in a public place without a valid third-party insurance policy, except as a passenger.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Chapter XI of the MV Act deals with insurance of motor vehicles against third-party risks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Exemption from Section 146: vehicles owned by Central or State Government used for government purposes not connected with commerce.
recall answer: Government vehicles used for non-commercial government purposes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: The Government may also exempt vehicles of a local authority or State Transport Undertaking if they keep a fund to meet claims.
recall answer: If it maintains a fund to meet liabilities.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: A paid employee driving an uninsured vehicle is not guilty unless they knew or had reason to believe there was no insurance.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Vehicles carrying dangerous or hazardous goods must also be insured under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 (added 2019).
recall answer: Under the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving an uninsured vehicle is punished under Section 196: first offence up to 3 months or ₹2,000, or both; later offences up to 3 months or ₹4,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Hit-and-run compensation (Section 161): ₹2 lakh for death and ₹50,000 for grievous hurt, paid from the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 164: compensation without proving fault: ₹5 lakh for death and ₹2.5 lakh for grievous hurt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Claims for compensation are decided by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) under Section 165.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 162 provides cashless treatment for accident victims during the golden hour. A 2025 central scheme gives up to ₹1.5 lakh per victim for 7 days.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Third-party insurance (Sec 146)
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Third-party insurance (Sec 146); standard diploma textbook

key text: Chapter XIII of the MV Act deals with offences, penalties and procedure (Sections 177 to 210). Fines were raised sharply in 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 177: general punishment when no separate penalty is given: ₹500 for the first offence and ₹1,500 for later offences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 177A: breaking the driving regulations made under Section 118 gives the same fine: ₹500 first, ₹1,500 later.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 178: travelling in a stage carriage without a ticket is fined ₹500. A conductor who fails to issue tickets or does their duty wrongly is also fined ₹500.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 178 also punishes refusing to ply a contract carriage (like a taxi or auto) or refusing to take passengers without good reason.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 179: disobeying lawful orders or obstructing an officer: ₹2,000. Withholding or giving false information: up to 1 month jail or ₹2,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 180: owner allowing an unauthorised person to drive: up to 3 months or ₹5,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 181: driving against Section 3 or 4 (no licence or under age): up to 3 months or ₹5,000, or both.
recall answer: Driving without licence or under age (Sec 3 or 4).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 182: driving while disqualified, or getting a licence while disqualified: up to 3 months or ₹10,000, or both. Conductor offences: up to 1 month or ₹10,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 182A: offences on construction, maintenance, sale and alteration of vehicles and parts. Manufacturer up to ₹100 crore; component maker up to ₹1 crore; illegal alteration ₹5,000 each.
recall answer: Construction, maintenance, sale and alteration offences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 183: speeding. Light motor vehicles: ₹1,000 to ₹2,000. Medium and heavy vehicles: ₹2,000 to ₹4,000. Repeat offence can lead to licence seizure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 184: dangerous driving includes jumping red lights, breaking stop signs, using hand-held phones, illegal overtaking and driving against traffic.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 184 penalty: first offence 6 months to 1 year jail, or ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 fine, or both. Repeat within 3 years: up to 2 years or ₹10,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 185: drunk driving means blood alcohol above 30 mg per 100 ml (by breath analyser), or driving under the influence of drugs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 185 penalty: first offence up to 6 months or ₹10,000, or both. Repeat within 3 years: up to 2 years or ₹15,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 186: driving when knowingly mentally or physically unfit: ₹1,000 first, ₹2,000 later.
recall answer: Driving when mentally or physically unfit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 187: failing duties after an accident (Sections 132, 133, 134): up to 6 months or ₹5,000, or both; later up to 1 year or ₹10,000.
recall answer: Offences relating to accident (duties not done).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook
