key text: Section 188: anyone who abets an offence under Sections 183, 184 or 189 gets the same punishment as for the offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 189: racing and speed trials on public roads without written consent of the State Government: first offence up to 3 months or ₹5,000, or both; later up to 1 year or ₹10,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 190(1): driving a vehicle with a defect likely to cause an accident: up to 3 months or ₹5,000; if it causes injury or damage, up to 6 months or ₹10,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 190(2): breaking road safety, noise or air pollution standards (such as no valid PUC): up to 3 months or ₹10,000, and licence disqualified for 3 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 190(3): carrying dangerous or hazardous goods without following the rules: up to 1 year or ₹10,000; later up to 3 years or ₹20,000.
recall answer: Carrying hazardous goods against the rules.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 192: using a vehicle without registration: first offence ₹2,000 to ₹5,000; later up to 1 year jail or ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 fine, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 192A: using a vehicle without a permit or against permit conditions: first offence up to ₹10,000 and up to 6 months.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 193: punishment of agents and canvassers (and aggregators) working without the licence required under Section 93.
recall answer: Agents, canvassers or aggregators without authority.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194: driving a vehicle beyond permissible weight: ₹20,000 plus ₹2,000 per extra tonne. Refusing to stop for weighing: ₹40,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194A: carrying excess passengers in a transport vehicle: ₹200 per extra passenger, and the extra passengers can be off-loaded.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194B(1): driving without a seat belt, or carrying passengers without seat belts: ₹1,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194B(2): carrying a child below 14 years not secured by a seat belt or child restraint system: ₹1,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194C: breaking motorcycle safety rules of Section 128 (like triple riding): ₹1,000 and 3 months disqualification.
recall answer: Safety measures for motorcycle drivers and pillion riders.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194D: not wearing a helmet: ₹1,000 and 3 months disqualification.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194E: not giving way to emergency vehicles: up to 6 months or ₹10,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 194F: needless or continuous horn use, or horn in a silence zone: ₹1,000 first, ₹2,000 later.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 196: driving an uninsured vehicle: up to 3 months or ₹2,000, or both; later ₹4,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 197: taking a vehicle without the owner's consent or lawful authority: up to 3 months or ₹5,000, or both.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 198: climbing on a stationary vehicle or tampering with its brakes or parts without lawful reason: ₹1,000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 198A: a contractor, consultant or road authority who fails to follow road design and maintenance standards, causing death or disability, is fined up to ₹1 lakh.
recall answer: Road authority, contractor or consultant failing road standards.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 199A: when a juvenile commits an offence, the guardian or owner is deemed guilty: up to 3 years jail and ₹25,000 fine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 199A, the vehicle's registration is cancelled for 12 months, and the juvenile cannot get a licence until age 25.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Defence under Section 199A: the guardian is not guilty if the offence was committed without their knowledge or they took all care to prevent it.
recall answer: Without knowledge, or after all due diligence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: A juvenile with a valid learner's or driving licence for that vehicle is outside Section 199A's guardian liability.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 200: certain offences can be compounded (settled by paying a fixed amount) by officers notified by the State, before or after prosecution starts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Drunk driving (Section 185) is not compoundable. It must go to court.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Compoundable offences include speeding (183), dangerous driving (184), no helmet (194D), no seat belt (194B), overloading (194), no insurance (196) and others listed in Section 200.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 202: a police officer in uniform may arrest without warrant a person who, in his presence, commits an offence under Section 184, 185 or 197.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 206: a police officer or authorised person can seize a document or registration mark that they believe is false.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 206(4): for offences under Sections 183, 184, 185, 189, 190, 194C, 194D or 194E, the officer shall seize the DL and send it to the licensing authority for disqualification under Section 19.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: When a DL is seized, the officer gives a temporary acknowledgement that lets the person drive until the case is decided.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 207: a police officer or authorised person can seize and detain a vehicle used without licence, registration or permit (against Sections 3, 4, 39 or 66).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: On seizing a vehicle under Section 207, the officer arranges safe custody and gives an acknowledgement. The vehicle is released when documents are produced or by order of the authority or court.
recall answer: On producing documents, by order of authority or court.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 208: summary disposal. For offences not punishable with jail, the court summons can let the accused plead guilty by post or electronically and pay the fine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 213: the State Government may set up a Motor Vehicles Department and appoint motor vehicles officers. They are public servants.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Powers under Section 213: make enquiries, stop vehicles and check documents, enter and search premises, examine persons, and seize records and documents.
recall answer: Stop vehicles and check papers; enter and search premises; seize records.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Under Section 213, a motor vehicles officer must be in uniform when exercising powers. The Central Government can prescribe minimum qualifications for these officers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: the syllabus prints Section 213 under 'Chapter XIV', which is the Miscellaneous chapter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook
Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Offences, penalties and procedure (Sec 177 to 213); standard diploma textbook

key text: Offences with 3-month DL disqualification: 190(2) pollution, 194C pillion rules, 194D helmet.
recall answer: No helmet (194D), triple riding (194C) or pollution (190(2)).

key text: The Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976 (KMVT Act) lets the State collect tax on motor vehicles used or kept for use in Kerala.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 2(e) of the KMVT Act defines purchase value: the value of the vehicle shown in the purchase invoice, including taxes, which is used to work out one-time tax.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 3: levy of tax. Tax is charged on every motor vehicle used or kept for use in Kerala, at rates fixed by the Government within the limits in the Schedule.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Private (non-transport) vehicles like motorcycles and cars pay a one-time tax for 15 years, worked out as a percentage of purchase value in slabs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transport vehicles usually pay tax quarterly (every three months) in advance. Rates depend on seats for passenger vehicles and on weight for goods vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 3A: levy of green tax on older vehicles, to discourage polluting vehicles. The money is used for environment-related measures.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 4: tax must be paid in advance by the registered owner or person in possession, and a licence (tax token or receipt) is issued.
recall answer: Registered owner or person in possession or control.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: KMVT Section 4 is 'Payment of tax and issue of licence'. The 'licence' here is the tax licence, not a driving licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 5: exemption from tax. The Government can exempt any class of vehicles, fully or partly, by notification.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: A vehicle not used for a period can avoid tax if the owner gives advance non-use intimation and follows the rules (such as surrendering documents).
recall answer: Give advance intimation of non-use as per rules.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 6: refund of tax. Tax paid can be refunded for periods the vehicle was not used, subject to conditions in the Act and rules.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Refund of one-time tax is also possible, in proportion, when a Kerala vehicle is moved and registered in another State, or is destroyed.
recall answer: Vehicle moved to another State, or destroyed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 7: additional tax. If a vehicle is altered or used in a way that needs a higher tax, the owner must pay the extra (difference) tax before using it so.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 10: officers of Police or MVD (of prescribed rank, in uniform) can stop a motor vehicle and keep it stationary to check tax payment and documents.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 11: if tax is not paid, the authorised officer can seize and detain the vehicle until the tax is paid. If still unpaid, the vehicle can be sold to recover the dues.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: When seizing under Section 11, the officer must arrange for the safety of passengers and goods in the vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 12: additional tax payable when tax is not paid in time. A penalty amount is added to the unpaid tax.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 13: unpaid tax and additional tax can be recovered as arrears of land revenue (under the Kerala Revenue Recovery Act).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section 26: escaped assessment. If tax was not assessed or was assessed too low, the taxation officer can assess and demand it later, after notice.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: Before demanding escaped tax under Section 26, the owner must be given notice and a chance to be heard.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: The taxation officer under the KMVT Act is usually the RTO or Joint RTO (Sub RTO).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: KMVT 2(e) purchase value, 3 levy, 3A green tax, 4 payment, 5 exemption, 6 refund, 7 additional tax, 10 stop, 11 seize, 12 late tax, 13 recovery, 26 escaped assessment.
recall answer: Recovery as arrears of land revenue.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: Section 7 'additional tax' is for changed use or alteration; Section 12 'additional tax' is a penalty for not paying tax in time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Kerala Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1976; standard diploma textbook

key text: A fluid is anything that flows: liquids and gases. It cannot keep its own shape.
recall answer: A substance that flows — liquid or gas.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Density (mass density) is mass per unit volume. Density = Mass / Volume. Unit: kg/m³. Symbol: ρ (rho).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific weight (weight density) is weight per unit volume. w = ρ × g. Unit: N/m³.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific volume is volume per unit mass. It is 1 / density. Unit: m³/kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific gravity (relative density) = density of the liquid / density of water. It has no unit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow — its inner friction. Thick fluid = high viscosity.
recall answer: Resistance to flow (internal friction of a fluid).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamic viscosity (μ) unit: N·s/m² or Pa·s. CGS unit: poise. 1 poise = 0.1 N·s/m².
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kinematic viscosity (ν) = dynamic viscosity / density. SI unit: m²/s. CGS unit: stoke.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Newton's law of viscosity: shear stress is proportional to velocity gradient. τ = μ × (du/dy).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Viscosity of liquids falls when heated. Viscosity of gases rises when heated.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compressibility is how much a fluid's volume shrinks under pressure. It is 1 / bulk modulus.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Surface tension is the pull on a liquid surface that makes it act like a stretched skin. Unit: N/m.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Capillarity: a liquid rises or falls in a thin tube. Water rises (wets glass). Mercury falls (does not wet glass).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Capillary rise h = 4σcosθ / (ρgd). Thinner tube → higher rise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Properties of fluids
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure = Force / Area. Unit: pascal (Pa) = 1 N/m². 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure in a liquid at depth h is p = ρgh. Pressure head h = p / (ρg).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Absolute pressure = Atmospheric pressure + Gauge pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vacuum pressure is pressure below atmospheric. Absolute = Atmospheric − Vacuum.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Standard atmospheric pressure = 101.325 kN/m² = 760 mm of mercury = 10.3 m of water.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pascal's law: pressure applied on a confined fluid is passed equally in all directions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: A piezometer is a simple open glass tube fixed to a pipe. Liquid rises in it to show pressure.
recall answer: No. Only small positive pressures of liquids.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A U-tube manometer has a liquid (often mercury) in a U-shaped tube. It measures high or negative pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A differential manometer measures the pressure difference between two points or two pipes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A Bourdon tube pressure gauge has a bent oval tube that straightens under pressure and turns a pointer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. A manometer measures fluid pressure in pipes or vessels.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ideal fluid: no viscosity and cannot be compressed. It does not exist in real life.

key text: Real fluid: has viscosity. All actual fluids are real fluids.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Newtonian fluid obeys Newton's law of viscosity: viscosity stays the same however fast you stir.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Non-Newtonian fluid does not obey Newton's law: its thickness changes when stirred or pushed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steady flow: speed and pressure at a point do not change with time. Unsteady flow: they change with time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Uniform flow: velocity is the same at every point along the flow. Non-uniform: velocity changes from point to point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Laminar flow: fluid moves in smooth parallel layers. Turbulent flow: fluid moves in a mixed, swirling way.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reynolds number decides the flow type in a pipe: below 2000 laminar, 2000–4000 transition, above 4000 turbulent.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Continuity equation: A₁V₁ = A₂V₂. Discharge stays the same through a pipe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Discharge (Q) = Area × Velocity. Unit: m³/s.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bernoulli's equation: pressure head + velocity head + datum head = constant, for an ideal flowing fluid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: A venturimeter measures discharge in a pipe. It has a converging part, a throat and a diverging part.
recall answer: Rate of flow (discharge) in a pipe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: An orifice is a small opening in the side or bottom of a tank. It is used to measure discharge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vena contracta is the narrowest part of a jet just after it leaves an orifice.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of discharge Cd = Cc × Cv. For an orifice, Cd is about 0.62.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: A notch is an opening at the top of a tank or channel wall, with the water surface below its top. Used to measure flow in open channels.

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Major loss in a pipe is loss of head due to friction along its length.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Minor losses come from bends, valves, sudden enlargement, sudden contraction, pipe entry and exit.
recall answer: Bends, valves, sudden enlargement/contraction, entry, exit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Darcy–Weisbach formula: hf = 4fLV² / (2gD). Loss grows with pipe length and with velocity squared.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chezy's formula: V = C √(m i). m = hydraulic mean depth, i = slope (loss of head per unit length).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic mean depth m = Area / wetted perimeter. For a full circular pipe, m = D/4.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Viscosity index (VI) shows how little an oil's viscosity changes with temperature. High VI = good oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oxidation stability is an oil's ability to resist reacting with oxygen and forming sludge and acids.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Demulsibility is an oil's ability to separate from water quickly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lubricity (oiliness) is an oil's ability to reduce friction and wear between surfaces.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rust prevention: hydraulic oil must protect steel parts from rusting, using added inhibitors.
recall answer: To protect metal parts from rust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pour point is the lowest temperature at which an oil will still flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flash point: lowest temperature at which oil vapour flashes briefly near a flame. Fire point: lowest temperature at which it keeps burning (at least 5 s). Fire point is higher.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Neutralisation number shows how acidic or basic an oil is. Rising acid number means the oil is getting old.

key text: A pump turns mechanical energy into hydraulic (pressure) energy. A turbine turns hydraulic energy into mechanical energy.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A centrifugal pump spins an impeller. The spinning throws water outward, building pressure. It is a rotodynamic pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A centrifugal pump must be primed (filled with liquid) before starting.
recall answer: Filling the pump and suction pipe with liquid before starting.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A reciprocating pump uses a piston moving to and fro inside a cylinder. It is a positive displacement pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Slip = theoretical discharge − actual discharge. % slip = (Qth − Qact)/Qth × 100.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Negative slip happens when actual discharge is more than theoretical. It occurs with long suction pipe, short delivery pipe and high speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Theoretical discharge of a single-acting reciprocating pump: Q = A L N / 60. Double acting: Q = 2 A L N / 60.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: An air vessel on a reciprocating pump gives a steady flow and saves power.
recall answer: Steady flow and saving power (less friction).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific speed of a pump: Ns = N√Q / H^(3/4). Of a turbine: Ns = N√P / H^(5/4).

key text: Impulse turbine: water hits buckets as a high-speed jet at atmospheric pressure. Example: Pelton wheel. Used for high head.

key text: Reaction turbine: water enters under pressure and both pressure and speed drop inside the runner. Examples: Francis (medium head), Kaplan (low head).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A draft tube is used in reaction turbines, not in impulse turbines. It recovers energy at the outlet.

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific weight of water = 9.81 kN/m³ (9810 N/m³).

key text: Cohesion is attraction between molecules of the same liquid. Adhesion is attraction between the liquid and another surface.

key text: Water's surface in a glass tube curves down in the middle (concave). Mercury's surface curves up (convex).

key text: Surface tension falls when temperature rises.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vapour pressure is the pressure of a liquid's vapour above it. It rises with temperature.

key text: Cavitation: when local pressure falls below vapour pressure, vapour bubbles form and then collapse violently.

key text: Liquids are taken as incompressible. Gases are compressible.

key text: Buoyancy (Archimedes): a body in a fluid feels an upward force equal to the weight of fluid it pushes aside.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Metacentre: a floating body is stable if the metacentre (M) is above its centre of gravity (G).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Fluid pressure and Pascal's law; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mercury is used in manometers because it is heavy, does not stick to glass, and does not evaporate easily.
recall answer: High density (also non-wetting, low vapour pressure).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: An inverted U-tube differential manometer uses a light liquid (or air) at the top. It measures small pressure differences.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A micromanometer (single-column with a large reservoir or inclined tube) measures very small pressures accurately.
recall answer: To read very small pressures more accurately.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A Pitot tube measures the velocity of flow at a point. It is an L-shaped tube facing the flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: A rotameter measures flow with a float inside a tapered glass tube. Higher flow lifts the float higher.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pressure measuring instruments; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ideal plastic (Bingham) fluid needs a minimum stress before it starts to flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thixotropic fluids get thinner the longer they are stirred. Example: paint, printer ink.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compressible fluid: density changes with pressure (gases). Incompressible fluid: density stays nearly constant (liquids).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of fluids
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Types of fluids; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compressible flow: density changes along the flow (gases at high speed). Incompressible flow: density stays constant (liquids).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rotational flow: fluid particles spin about their own axis. Irrotational flow: they do not spin.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: One-dimensional flow: velocity changes in one direction only. Two- and three-dimensional flows change in more directions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: A streamline is an imaginary line that shows the direction of flow at every point. Streamlines never cross.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: In Bernoulli's equation the three heads are: pressure head p/ρg, velocity (kinetic) head V²/2g and datum (potential) head z.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bernoulli's equation assumes: ideal (non-viscous), incompressible, steady flow along a streamline.
recall answer: Ideal, incompressible, steady flow along a streamline.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic gradient line (HGL) joins pressure + datum heads. Total energy line (TEL) is higher than HGL by V²/2g.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Venturimeter's coefficient of discharge is high, about 0.96–0.98. Orifice meter's is low, about 0.6.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a venturimeter, the converging cone is short and the diverging cone is long (angle about 5–7°).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: An orifice meter is a thin plate with a hole fitted in a pipe. It is cheaper but loses more energy than a venturimeter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of contraction Cc = jet area at vena contracta / orifice area (about 0.64). Coefficient of velocity Cv ≈ 0.97–0.99.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: A mouthpiece is a short tube (2–3 times its diameter) fitted to an orifice. It increases discharge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Discharge over a rectangular notch Q ∝ H^(3/2). Over a triangular (V) notch Q ∝ H^(5/2).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: A weir is a large notch, usually built of masonry across a river or canal. A notch is small and made of metal plate.
recall answer: Notch: small, metal plate. Weir: large, masonry structure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Momentum equation: force on a fluid = rate of change of momentum. Used to find force of a jet on a plate.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook
