source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flow types, orifice, notch, venturimeter, continuity; standard diploma textbook

key text: Loss due to sudden enlargement = (V₁ − V₂)² / 2g.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Loss at pipe entrance = 0.5 V²/2g. Loss at pipe exit = V²/2g.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Loss due to sudden contraction ≈ 0.5 V₂²/2g (V₂ = velocity in the smaller pipe).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: For laminar flow, friction factor f = 16/Re (or Darcy f' = 64/Re).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hagen–Poiseuille equation gives head loss in laminar pipe flow: hf = 32 μ V L / (ρ g D²).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Moody diagram links friction factor with Reynolds number and pipe roughness for turbulent flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Water hammer is a pressure surge when a valve in a pipe is closed suddenly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pipes in series: same discharge, head losses add. Pipes in parallel: same head loss, discharges add.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Head losses, Darcy and Chezy formulas; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cloud point is the temperature at which wax crystals first make the oil look cloudy. It is a little above the pour point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Foam resistance: a good hydraulic oil must not foam. Air bubbles make the system spongy.
recall answer: Air bubbles make the system spongy and weak.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Main jobs of a hydraulic oil: pass power, lubricate, seal, cool and protect from rust.
recall answer: To transmit power (also lubricate, seal, cool).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: SAE number shows the viscosity grade of engine oil. 'W' means winter grade. In 20W-40, the oil acts like SAE 20 when cold and SAE 40 when hot.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic brake fluid is not mineral oil. It is glycol based (DOT 3, DOT 4).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake fluid absorbs moisture from air (hygroscopic). This lowers its boiling point, so it is changed regularly.
recall answer: It absorbs water, which lowers its boiling point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Properties of hydraulic oils; standard diploma textbook

key text: Main parts of a centrifugal pump: impeller, casing, suction pipe with foot valve and strainer, delivery pipe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A volute casing is spiral-shaped; its area grows towards the outlet. It turns velocity into pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Manometric head of a centrifugal pump = actual head the pump develops (static head + losses + exit velocity head).
recall answer: The total head the pump must develop.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Manometric efficiency = manometric head / head given by the impeller. Overall efficiency = water power / shaft power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pumps in series increase head. Pumps in parallel increase discharge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: NPSH (net positive suction head) must be enough at the pump inlet, or cavitation starts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A centrifugal pump suits large flow at low or medium head. A reciprocating pump suits small flow at high head.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gear pumps and vane pumps are rotary positive displacement pumps. They are used for oil and power steering.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pelton wheel parts: nozzle with spear, runner with buckets, casing, breaking jet. Buckets have a splitter in the middle.
recall answer: To divide the jet into two equal parts (avoid side thrust).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Best speed ratio of a Pelton wheel is about 0.46 (bucket speed ≈ half the jet speed).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Francis turbine is an inward mixed-flow reaction turbine with fixed runner blades and guide vanes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kaplan turbine is an axial-flow reaction turbine with adjustable runner blades. A propeller turbine has fixed blades.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific speed ranges: Pelton low (about 10–35), Francis medium (about 60–300), Kaplan high (300–1000).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Impulse vs reaction: impulse works at atmospheric pressure, partly filled, no draft tube. Reaction runs full of water under pressure, with a draft tube.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Governing of a turbine keeps its speed constant when load changes, by controlling the water flow.
recall answer: To keep speed constant as load changes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: A hydraulic ram lifts part of a water flow to a higher level using water hammer. It needs no outside power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic accumulator stores hydraulic energy (pressurised liquid) for later use.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic intensifier increases the pressure of a liquid using a large and a small piston.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: slip of a reciprocating pump
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Pumps and turbines; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermodynamics is the study of heat, work and energy, and how one changes into another.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: A system is the part we study. Everything outside it is the surroundings. The line between them is the boundary.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Closed system: mass does not cross, energy can. Open system: both mass and energy cross. Isolated system: neither crosses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Intensive properties do not depend on mass (pressure, temperature, density). Extensive properties depend on mass (volume, energy, mass).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat and work are energy in transit. They are path functions, not properties.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Absolute temperature: K = °C + 273.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific heat is the heat needed to raise 1 kg of a substance by 1°C. For gases there are two: cp (constant pressure) and cv (constant volume).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: For air: cp = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, cv = 0.718 kJ/kg·K, γ = cp/cv = 1.4, R = cp − cv = 0.287 kJ/kg·K.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Internal energy is energy stored in a substance due to its molecules' motion. For an ideal gas it depends only on temperature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Enthalpy H = U + pV. It is the total heat content of a flowing fluid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Entropy is a measure of disorder. In a reversible adiabatic process entropy stays constant.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Boyle's law: pV = constant at constant temperature. Charles's law: V/T = constant at constant pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Basic terms of thermodynamics
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Basic terms of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Zeroth law: if A and B are each in thermal balance with C, then A and B are in thermal balance with each other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: First law: energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: First law for a closed system: Q = ΔU + W (heat supplied = rise in internal energy + work done).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: For a cycle, net heat = net work (∮δQ = ∮δW).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: A perpetual motion machine of the first kind (PMM-1) makes work without any energy input. The first law says it is impossible.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Second law (Kelvin–Planck): no engine working in a cycle can turn all heat into work. Some heat must go to a cold sink.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Second law (Clausius): heat cannot flow from a cold body to a hot body by itself without outside work.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: PMM-2 is an engine that turns all heat into work with one heat source. The second law says it is impossible.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Third law: entropy of a perfect crystal at absolute zero (0 K) is zero.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat engine efficiency η = Work output / Heat supplied = 1 − Q₂/Q₁.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: COP of a refrigerator = heat removed / work input. COP of a heat pump = heat delivered / work input = COP(ref) + 1.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Laws of thermodynamics
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant volume (isochoric) process: volume does not change, so no work is done (W = 0).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant pressure (isobaric) process: W = p (V₂ − V₁).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Isothermal process: temperature stays constant, pV = constant. W = p₁V₁ ln(V₂/V₁).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: In an isothermal process of an ideal gas, ΔU = 0, so Q = W.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Adiabatic process: no heat crosses the boundary (Q = 0). Reversible adiabatic is called isentropic: pV^γ = constant.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Work in an adiabatic process W = (p₁V₁ − p₂V₂)/(γ − 1). Polytropic: W = (p₁V₁ − p₂V₂)/(n − 1).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Polytropic process: pVⁿ = constant. n = 0 constant pressure, n = 1 isothermal, n = γ adiabatic, n = ∞ constant volume.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: On a PV diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Area under a curve on a PV diagram = work done. Area enclosed by a cycle = net work of the cycle.
recall answer: Net work done in the cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Throttling process: fluid passes through a narrow valve; enthalpy stays constant (h₁ = h₂) and no work is done.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Free expansion: gas expands into vacuum. Work done = 0 and heat = 0.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermodynamic processes and PV diagrams; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air standard cycle assumptions: working fluid is air (ideal gas), constant specific heats, heat added from outside, processes reversible, no intake or exhaust losses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carnot cycle: two isothermal and two adiabatic (isentropic) processes. It has the highest possible efficiency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carnot efficiency η = 1 − T₂/T₁ (temperatures in kelvin).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carnot cycle is not used in real engines. Isothermal processes are too slow and adiabatic ones too fast to achieve in one engine.
recall answer: No — it is only a standard for comparison.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Otto cycle (petrol engine): 2 adiabatic + 2 constant volume processes. Heat is added at constant volume.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Otto cycle efficiency η = 1 − 1/r^(γ−1). r = compression ratio.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel cycle: 2 adiabatic, 1 constant pressure (heat added) and 1 constant volume (heat rejected).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cut-off ratio ρ = V₃/V₂ in a Diesel cycle: volume when fuel injection stops ÷ clearance volume. Larger cut-off ratio lowers efficiency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: For the same compression ratio, Otto is more efficient than Diesel. For the same maximum pressure, Diesel is more efficient.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dual combustion (mixed or limited pressure) cycle: heat is added partly at constant volume and partly at constant pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Joule (Brayton) cycle: 2 adiabatic and 2 constant pressure processes. Used in gas turbines and jet engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Joule cycle efficiency η = 1 − 1/rp^((γ−1)/γ). rp = pressure ratio.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compression ratio r = total cylinder volume / clearance volume = (Vs + Vc)/Vc.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol engines use low compression ratios (about 8–12) to avoid knocking. Diesel engines need high ratios (about 14–22) to self-ignite fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stirling cycle: 2 isothermal and 2 constant volume processes, with a regenerator. Ericsson cycle: 2 isothermal and 2 constant pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mean effective pressure (MEP) = net work of cycle / swept volume.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: Otto cycle efficiency
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: Carnot efficiency
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air standard cycles
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: An internal combustion (IC) engine burns fuel inside the cylinder. An external combustion engine burns fuel outside (e.g. steam engine).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol engine = spark ignition (SI). Diesel engine = compression ignition (CI).
recall answer: By heat of compressed air (compression ignition).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Four-stroke engine strokes in order: suction, compression, power, exhaust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: A four-stroke engine gives one power stroke every 2 revolutions of the crankshaft. A two-stroke engine gives one every revolution.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a four-stroke engine, the camshaft turns at half the crankshaft speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a petrol engine, the suction stroke draws in an air–petrol mixture. In a diesel engine, it draws in air only.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-stroke engines use ports (holes in the cylinder wall) instead of valves: inlet, transfer and exhaust ports.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a two-stroke petrol engine, the crankcase is sealed and used to pre-compress the fresh mixture.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Scavenging is pushing out burnt gases with fresh charge in a two-stroke engine.
recall answer: Clearing exhaust gases from the cylinder using fresh charge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: A deflector-top piston directs fresh charge upward in cross-scavenged two-stroke engines.
recall answer: To guide fresh charge up and reduce loss through the exhaust port.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-stroke vs four-stroke: two-stroke is lighter, simpler and more powerful for its size, but uses more fuel and pollutes more.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-stroke petrol engines are lubricated by mixing oil with petrol (petroil), about 2–3%.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel engines are heavier and costlier but more fuel-efficient and give more torque than petrol engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: TDC (top dead centre) is the top-most piston position. BDC (bottom dead centre) is the bottom-most.
recall answer: Top dead centre — piston's highest position.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stroke = distance between TDC and BDC = 2 × crank radius. Bore = cylinder diameter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Swept volume Vs = (π/4) × D² × L. Engine capacity (cc) = swept volume × number of cylinders.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Square engine: bore = stroke. Over-square (short stroke): bore > stroke. Under-square (long stroke): bore < stroke.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clearance volume is the space left above the piston at TDC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve timing diagram shows, in crank degrees, when inlet and exhaust valves open and close.
recall answer: Crank angles at which valves open and close.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inlet valve opens about 10–20° before TDC and closes about 30–50° after BDC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust valve opens about 40–50° before BDC and closes about 10–20° after TDC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve overlap is the period when both inlet and exhaust valves are open together, near TDC.
recall answer: During valve overlap, near TDC (end of exhaust, start of suction).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve lead: valve opens before the dead centre. Valve lag: valve closes after the dead centre.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition timing: the spark occurs before TDC (spark advance). In diesel engines, injection starts before TDC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Knocking in petrol engines (detonation) is sudden self-ignition of the last part of the mixture, causing a metallic noise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Octane number rates petrol's anti-knock quality (iso-octane = 100, n-heptane = 0). Cetane number rates diesel's ignition quality (cetane = 100).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel knock is caused by a long ignition delay: too much fuel collects before burning, then explodes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Things that reduce petrol knock lead to more diesel knock, and vice versa. For example, high compression ratio reduces diesel knock but increases petrol knock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: On the PV diagram of an actual four-stroke engine, the small negative loop at the bottom is the pumping loss loop (suction and exhaust).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Firing order of a common 4-cylinder in-line engine: 1-3-4-2 (or 1-2-4-3).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wankel (rotary) engine uses a triangular rotor instead of a piston.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Indicated power (IP) is power developed by the gas inside the cylinder. IP = p_m L A n k / 60 (n = power strokes per minute).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake power (BP) is the useful power at the crankshaft. BP = 2πNT / 60.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frictional power FP = IP − BP.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mechanical efficiency ηm = BP / IP.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Indicated thermal efficiency = IP / (fuel mass per second × calorific value).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake thermal efficiency = BP / (mf × CV). Brake thermal efficiency = mechanical efficiency × indicated thermal efficiency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Relative efficiency (efficiency ratio) = actual thermal efficiency / air standard efficiency.
recall answer: Actual thermal efficiency ÷ air standard efficiency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific fuel consumption (SFC) = fuel used per hour / brake power. Unit: kg/kWh. Lower SFC = better engine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Volumetric efficiency = actual volume of air drawn in / swept volume (at intake conditions).
recall answer: Actual air drawn in with swept volume.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: A dynamometer measures brake power. Types: rope brake, Prony brake (absorption), hydraulic, eddy current, and transmission dynamometers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engine indicator draws the actual PV (indicator) diagram of a running engine. Its area gives indicated work.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Morse test finds IP of a multi-cylinder engine. Each cylinder is cut off in turn, and the fall in BP gives that cylinder's IP.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: In the Morse test, IP of one cylinder = total BP − BP with that cylinder cut off. Sum for all cylinders gives engine IP.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Willan's line method (fuel rate extrapolation) finds frictional power of a diesel engine by plotting fuel consumption against BP and extending the line to zero fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motoring test: the engine is driven by an electric motor without firing; motor power needed = frictional power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat balance sheet shows where fuel heat goes: brake power, cooling water, exhaust gases and unaccounted losses.
recall answer: BP, cooling water, exhaust, unaccounted losses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: A typical petrol engine turns only about 25–30% of fuel heat into brake power. About 30% goes to cooling and about 35% to exhaust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Calorific value is the heat released by burning 1 kg of fuel. Petrol and diesel are about 42–44 MJ/kg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stoichiometric (chemically correct) air–fuel ratio for petrol is about 14.7 : 1 by mass.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque is turning force at the crankshaft (N·m). Power = torque × speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: 1 metric horsepower = 735.5 W. 1 kW ≈ 1.36 metric hp.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: mechanical efficiency
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: brake power
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: IC engine performance and testing
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: An air compressor takes in air at low pressure and delivers it at high pressure.
recall answer: Raises the pressure of air (or gas).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Uses of compressed air in vehicles: air brakes, air suspension, tyre inflation, door opening in buses, horns, paint spraying in workshops.
recall answer: Air brakes (also tyre inflation, air suspension, doors).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of compressors: reciprocating (piston), rotary (vane, screw, lobe/roots), centrifugal and axial.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single acting compressor: air is compressed on one side of the piston. Double acting: on both sides.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single stage compressor: air compressed to final pressure in one cylinder. Multi-stage: in two or more cylinders with intercooling.
recall answer: Saves work and keeps temperature low (with intercooling).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: An intercooler cools air between stages of a multi-stage compressor.
recall answer: To cool air between compression stages.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Perfect intercooling: air is cooled back to its starting temperature after each stage.
recall answer: Cooling air to initial (suction) temperature after each stage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: For least work in a two-stage compressor, intermediate pressure p₂ = √(p₁ × p₃).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compression work is least for isothermal compression and most for adiabatic compression.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Isothermal efficiency of a compressor = isothermal work / actual work.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Volumetric efficiency of a reciprocating compressor falls as clearance volume and pressure ratio rise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Free air delivered (FAD) is the compressed air output, expressed as volume at atmospheric conditions.
recall answer: Free air delivered — output volume at atmospheric conditions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Roots blower (lobe compressor) has no internal compression; it moves air and pressure rises at delivery. Used as superchargers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centrifugal compressors (turbochargers) use a fast-spinning impeller to throw air outward and raise its pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air compressors
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat moves in three ways: conduction, convection and radiation.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Conduction is heat passing through a solid from particle to particle, with no movement of the material.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Convection is heat carried by moving fluid (liquid or gas).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Natural (free) convection: fluid moves due to density difference. Forced convection: a fan or pump moves the fluid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radiation is heat travelling as electromagnetic waves. It needs no medium and can cross vacuum.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fourier's law of conduction: Q = −k A (dT/dx). Heat flow is proportional to area and temperature gradient.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermal conductivity (k) is a material's ability to conduct heat. Unit: W/m·K.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Silver and copper have very high thermal conductivity. Air, wood and glass wool have low k (insulators).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Newton's law of cooling: convection heat Q = h A (Ts − T∞). h = heat transfer coefficient (W/m²K).
recall answer: Newton's law of cooling, Q = hAΔT.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stefan–Boltzmann law: radiation energy E = σ T⁴. σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/m²K⁴.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: A black body absorbs all radiation falling on it and is the best emitter. Emissivity of a black body = 1.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kirchhoff's law: at thermal equilibrium, emissivity of a body equals its absorptivity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermal resistance of a plane wall R = L/(kA). Walls in series: resistances add.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat exchanger types: parallel flow (both fluids same direction) and counter flow (opposite directions). Counter flow is more effective.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fins are extended surfaces that increase heat transfer area.
recall answer: To increase surface area for heat loss.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat transfer
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engines are classified by fuel (petrol, diesel, CNG, LPG), ignition (SI, CI), strokes (2, 4), cooling (air, water), cylinder layout (inline, V, flat/opposed, radial) and valve position.
recall answer: Fuel, ignition, strokes, cooling, cylinder arrangement, valve position.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: V-engine: two rows of cylinders in a V shape on one crankshaft. Flat (boxer): two rows lying opposite each other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol engine has a spark plug and carburettor or petrol injector. Diesel engine has a fuel injection pump and injector, and no spark plug.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol engine power is controlled by a throttle valve (quantity governing). Diesel engine power is controlled by the amount of fuel injected (quality governing).
recall answer: By changing the quantity of fuel injected (quality governing).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel engines run at lower speeds than petrol engines and have heavier parts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition delay in a diesel engine is the time between start of injection and start of combustion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stages of combustion in a CI engine: ignition delay, rapid (uncontrolled) combustion, controlled combustion, after-burning.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stages of combustion in an SI engine: ignition lag (preparation), flame propagation, after-burning.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pre-ignition is ignition of the mixture before the spark, by a hot spot such as a glowing carbon deposit or overheated plug.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Running-on (dieseling) is when a petrol engine keeps running after the ignition is switched off.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tetra-ethyl lead (TEL) was once added to petrol to stop knocking. It is now banned because lead is poisonous and damages catalytic converters.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Supercharging is forcing more air into the cylinder than it would draw by itself. Turbocharger uses exhaust gas; supercharger is driven by the engine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel combustion chambers: direct injection (open chamber) and indirect injection (pre-combustion chamber, swirl chamber).
recall answer: Direct injection (open) and indirect (pre-chamber, swirl chamber).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Glow plugs heat the combustion chamber of indirect injection diesel engines for easy cold starting.
recall answer: To help cold starting of diesel engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Squish is the squeezing of mixture out from between piston crown and head near TDC. Swirl is the rotating motion of air in the cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mean piston speed = 2 L N / 60 (m/s).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Power strokes per minute: four-stroke n = N/2; two-stroke n = N (N = rpm).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel for SI engines must be volatile (evaporate easily). Fuel for CI engines must have good ignition quality and suitable viscosity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: CNG has high octane (about 120) and suits SI engines. LPG is mainly propane and butane.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: CNG is mostly methane, stored at about 200 bar in cylinders.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Two-stroke and four-stroke engines, valve timing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake mean effective pressure (bmep) = BP related to swept volume. imep relates to IP. bmep = ηm × imep.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engine performance curves plot BP, torque and SFC against speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air consumption is measured with an air box and orifice, which steadies the pulsing intake flow.
recall answer: Air box with an orifice and manometer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel consumption is measured with a burette: time taken to use a known volume (e.g. 50 cc) of fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Indicated thermal efficiency is always higher than brake thermal efficiency.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust gas analysers measure CO, HC, CO₂ and O₂ in petrol exhaust. Smoke meters measure diesel smoke opacity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — IC engine performance and testing; standard diploma textbook

key text: Good insulators: asbestos (now avoided), glass wool, mineral wool, cork, thermocol.
recall answer: It traps still air, which conducts heat poorly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat transfer in an engine: gas to cylinder wall by convection and radiation, through wall by conduction, wall to coolant by convection.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermos flask: double glass walls with vacuum between (stops conduction and convection) and silvered surfaces (stop radiation).
recall answer: To reduce heat transfer by radiation.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Heat transfer; standard diploma textbook

key text: Otto cycle efficiency rises with compression ratio, but petrol engines cannot go very high because of knocking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel cycle efficiency η = 1 − (1/r^(γ−1)) × [(ρ^γ − 1)/(γ(ρ − 1))].
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gas turbines can use regeneration, reheating and intercooling to raise efficiency and work output.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air standard cycles; standard diploma textbook

key text: A heat engine needs: a hot source, a working fluid, and a cold sink.
recall answer: Hot source, working substance, cold sink.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reversible process: can be reversed with no change left in system or surroundings. All real processes are irreversible.
recall answer: Friction (or heat flow across finite temperature difference, mixing).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Laws of thermodynamics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compressor parts: cylinder, piston, inlet and delivery valves (reed or plate type), unloader, air receiver tank, safety valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: A governor (unloader) in a vehicle air compressor stops compression when tank pressure reaches its limit (about 7–8 bar).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Air compressors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Load is the outside force acting on a body. Stress is the inside resisting force per unit area. Stress = Load / Area.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Unit of stress: N/m² (pascal). In engineering we often use N/mm² = MPa.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strain is change in length divided by original length. Strain = δL / L. It has no unit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tensile stress: forces pull the body and it gets longer. Compressive stress: forces push and it gets shorter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shear stress: two equal, opposite forces act along (parallel to) a surface and try to slide one part over the other. τ = P / A.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shear strain is the angle change (in radians) produced by shear stress. Symbol φ.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Longitudinal strain is strain along the load. Lateral strain is strain at right angles to the load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Poisson's ratio (μ or 1/m) = lateral strain / longitudinal strain. For steel about 0.25–0.3.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Poisson's ratio lies between 0 and 0.5 for usual materials. Cork ≈ 0, rubber ≈ 0.5.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Volumetric strain = change in volume / original volume. For a bar in tension: εv = ε (1 − 2μ).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Direct (normal) stress acts at right angles to the surface. Shear stress acts along the surface.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Complementary shear stress: shear stress on one plane always comes with an equal shear stress on the plane at right angles.
recall answer: Equal shear stress on the perpendicular plane.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bearing (crushing) stress is compressive stress where two parts press on each other. In a rivet: σc = P / (d × t).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strain energy is energy stored in a body when it is strained. Resilience is strain energy stored per unit volume up to the elastic limit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strain energy U = σ² V / (2E). Proof resilience is maximum strain energy stored up to the elastic limit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: A suddenly applied load causes twice the stress of the same load applied gradually.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stress and strain
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: A stress–strain diagram is drawn from a tensile test on a universal testing machine (UTM).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Points on the mild steel diagram in order: limit of proportionality, elastic limit, upper yield point, lower yield point, ultimate stress, breaking point.
recall answer: Proportional limit, elastic limit, upper yield, lower yield, ultimate, breaking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Limit of proportionality: up to this point stress is directly proportional to strain (straight line).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Elastic limit: the highest stress after which the material still returns to its original shape when the load is removed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Yield point: the material stretches a lot with almost no increase in load. Mild steel has a clear upper and lower yield point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ultimate stress is the maximum stress a material can take. It is the highest point on the curve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Necking: after ultimate stress, a ductile bar gets thinner at one spot and breaks there.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Breaking stress (nominal) is lower than ultimate stress on the engineering curve, because the original area is used.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ductile material stretches a lot before breaking (mild steel, copper, aluminium). Brittle material breaks with very little stretch (cast iron, glass, concrete).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brittle materials have no clear yield point. Their curve is nearly straight to fracture.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Proof stress (0.2% offset) is used as yield strength for materials without a clear yield point, like aluminium and high-tensile steel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Percentage elongation and percentage reduction in area measure ductility.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Working stress (allowable stress) is the safe stress used in design. It is kept well below the failure stress.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Factor of safety = ultimate stress / working stress (or yield stress / working stress for ductile metals).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Factor of safety is always more than 1. It is higher for brittle materials and shock loads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Elasticity: returns to shape after load. Plasticity: keeps the new shape. Malleability: can be hammered into sheets. Toughness: absorbs energy before breaking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hardness is resistance to scratching, wear and indentation. Tests: Brinell, Rockwell, Vickers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Impact tests (Izod, Charpy) measure toughness — energy absorbed when a notched specimen is broken by a swinging hammer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fatigue: failure under repeated (cyclic) loading at stress below the ultimate strength. Endurance limit is the stress below which it never fails.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Creep: slow permanent stretching under a constant load over a long time, especially at high temperature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: stress and factor of safety
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Stress–strain diagram and factor of safety; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hooke's law: within the elastic limit, stress is directly proportional to strain.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Young's modulus E = tensile (or compressive) stress / linear strain. Steel E ≈ 200 GPa (2 × 10⁵ N/mm²).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Modulus of rigidity G (shear modulus) = shear stress / shear strain. Steel G ≈ 80 GPa.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bulk modulus K = direct stress (equal on all sides) / volumetric strain.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Relations: E = 2G(1 + μ) and E = 3K(1 − 2μ).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Combined relation: E = 9KG / (3K + G).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Elongation of a bar: δL = P L / (A E).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Principle of superposition: total effect of many loads = sum of effects of each load acting alone (within elastic limit).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bar of varying (stepped) section: total δL = (P/E)(L₁/A₁ + L₂/A₂ + ...).
recall answer: Add elongations of each part: Σ PL/(AE).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Uniformly tapering circular bar: δL = 4PL / (π E d₁ d₂).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Elongation of a bar due to its own weight = w L² / (2E) = W L / (2AE).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Composite section: two materials joined to share a load. Both have the same strain; loads add: P = P₁ + P₂.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a composite bar, σ₁/E₁ = σ₂/E₂. The stiffer material carries more stress.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Hooke's law, elastic constants, varying and composite sections; standard diploma textbook

key text: Metals expand when heated and shrink when cooled.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Free expansion δL = α L ΔT. α = coefficient of linear expansion (per °C).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: If expansion is prevented, thermal stress is set up: σ = E α ΔT.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermal stress does not depend on the length or area of the bar.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heated and restrained → compressive stress. Cooled and restrained → tensile stress.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: If supports yield by δ, thermal stress σ = E (αLΔT − δ) / L.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Composite bar heated: material with higher α goes into compression; lower α goes into tension.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a composite bar with temperature change, compressive force in one = tensile force in the other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of linear expansion: aluminium ≈ 23, copper ≈ 17, steel ≈ 12 (all × 10⁻⁶ /°C).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Area expansion coefficient β ≈ 2α. Volume expansion coefficient γ ≈ 3α.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shrink fit: a part is heated to expand, fitted on a shaft, and grips tightly as it cools.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: thermal stress
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermal stress and strain
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Thermal stress and strain; standard diploma textbook

key text: Friction is the force that resists sliding between two surfaces in contact. It acts opposite to motion.
recall answer: Opposite to motion (or tendency of motion).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Static friction acts before motion starts. Dynamic (kinetic) friction acts during motion. Static friction is greater.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Limiting friction is the maximum static friction just before sliding begins.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rolling friction is much smaller than sliding friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of friction μ = F / R (friction force / normal reaction). It has no unit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Laws of dry friction: friction ∝ normal reaction; it does not depend on contact area; it depends on the nature of surfaces; it acts opposite to motion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kinetic friction is almost independent of speed at low speeds.
recall answer: No — nearly constant at low speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Angle of friction φ: tan φ = μ. Angle of repose: the steepest slope on which a body rests without sliding. Angle of repose = angle of friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluid (viscous) friction occurs between layers of a fluid or between lubricated surfaces. It is much smaller than dry friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Boundary friction happens when the oil film is very thin, as at engine start-up.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Force to pull a body up a rough slope P = W (sin α + μ cos α), with P parallel to the slope.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Friction is useful in brakes, clutches, belts, tyres, nuts and bolts, and walking. It is harmful in bearings, pistons and gears.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Friction
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Friction; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centre of gravity (CG) is the point where the whole weight of a body seems to act.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centroid is the geometric centre of a plane area. For a uniform body, centroid and CG are the same point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centroid of a triangle is at h/3 from the base. Of a semicircle: 4r/(3π) from the diameter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: A vehicle with a low CG is more stable and less likely to overturn.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Moment of inertia (second moment of area) shows how an area is spread around an axis. Unit: mm⁴ (area), kg·m² (mass).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: MI of a rectangle about its centroid axis: I = b d³ / 12. About its base: b d³ / 3.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: MI of a circle about its diameter: I = π d⁴ / 64. Polar MI: J = π d⁴ / 32.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: MI of a triangle about its base = b h³ / 12; about its centroidal axis = b h³ / 36.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Parallel axis theorem: I = Ig + A h². Perpendicular axis theorem: Iz = Ix + Iy (for plane areas).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radius of gyration k = √(I / A). It is the distance at which all area could be packed to give the same MI.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: I-sections are used for beams and chassis frames because most material is far from the neutral axis, giving high MI for low weight.
recall answer: High MI (stiffness) with less material and weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centre of gravity and moment of inertia
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Centre of gravity and moment of inertia; standard diploma textbook

key text: A beam is a horizontal member that carries loads at right angles to its length and bends.
recall answer: A member carrying transverse loads, which bends.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cantilever beam: fixed at one end, free at the other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Simply supported beam: rests freely on supports at both ends.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other beams: overhanging (extends past a support), fixed (both ends fixed), continuous (more than two supports), propped cantilever.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Point load: acts at a single point. Uniformly distributed load (UDL): spread evenly along a length, in N/m.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shear force at a section = algebraic sum of vertical forces on one side of it.
recall answer: All vertical forces on one side of the section.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bending moment at a section = algebraic sum of moments of forces on one side about that section.
recall answer: Sum of moments of forces on one side about the section.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bending moment is maximum where shear force is zero or changes sign.
recall answer: Where shear force is zero (changes sign).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cantilever with point load W at free end: max SF = W, max BM = W L at the fixed end.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cantilever with UDL w over length L: max SF = wL, max BM = wL²/2 at the fixed end.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Simply supported beam with central point load W: reactions W/2 each, max BM = WL/4 at the centre.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Simply supported beam with UDL w: reactions wL/2, max BM = wL²/8 at the centre.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: SFD shape: point loads give horizontal steps; UDL gives a sloping straight line. BMD: point loads give straight lines; UDL gives a parabola.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sagging BM (beam bends like a smile, concave up) is positive. Hogging BM (like a frown) is negative.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Point of contraflexure: where bending moment changes sign (becomes zero).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bending equation: M/I = σ/y = E/R.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Neutral axis: the line in a bent beam with zero stress. Above it is compression, below it tension (for sagging).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Section modulus Z = I / y_max. Max bending stress σ = M / Z. Rectangle: Z = b d² / 6.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Max deflection: cantilever end load WL³/3EI; simply supported central load WL³/48EI; simply supported UDL 5wL⁴/384EI.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torsion equation: T/J = τ/r = Gθ/L.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: A hollow shaft is stronger and stiffer than a solid shaft of the same weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: simply supported beam
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: cantilever with UDL
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Beams, shear force and bending moment; standard diploma textbook

key text: A rivet is a permanent fastener: a round rod with a head, put through holes in plates, and the other end hammered into a second head.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Parts of a rivet: head, shank (body) and tail (point).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rivet head types: snap (cup/button), pan, countersunk, conical. Countersunk heads sit flush with the surface.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lap joint: one plate overlaps the other and they are riveted together.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Butt joint: plates meet end to end and are joined by one or two cover (strap) plates.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single riveted: one row of rivets. Double riveted: two rows. Arrangement can be chain (in line) or zig-zag (staggered).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pitch (p) is the distance between centres of adjacent rivets in a row. Margin is the distance from rivet centre to plate edge (about 1.5d).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Back pitch is the distance between rows. Diagonal pitch is the distance between rivets in adjacent rows in zig-zag riveting.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ways a riveted joint can fail: shearing of rivets, tearing of plate between rivets, crushing of rivets or plate, tearing of plate at the edge.
recall answer: Rivet shearing, plate tearing, crushing, edge tearing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tearing strength of plate per pitch length: Pt = (p − d) t σt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shearing strength of a rivet in single shear: Ps = (π/4) d² τ. In double shear: Ps = 2 × (π/4) d² τ (theoretically).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crushing strength: Pc = d × t × σc (per rivet).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strength of the riveted joint = the least of tearing, shearing and crushing strengths.
recall answer: The least of Pt, Ps and Pc.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Efficiency of a riveted joint = least strength / strength of the solid plate (p × t × σt).
recall answer: Least of (Pt, Ps, Pc) ÷ (p t σt).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Unwin's formula gives rivet diameter: d = 6√t (mm), when t > 8 mm.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Caulking and fullering make riveted joints leak-proof, as in boilers. Fullering is the better method.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rivets are commonly made of mild steel, wrought iron, copper or aluminium.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pop (blind) rivets are fixed from one side only, using a rivet gun.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook
