source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Riveted joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: A bolt is a threaded rod with a head, used with a nut. It is a temporary (removable) fastener.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types: through bolt (with nut), tap bolt (screwed into a threaded hole), stud (threaded both ends), cap screw, set screw.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bolt heads: hexagonal (most common), square, eye bolt (for lifting), T-bolt, hook bolt, foundation bolt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Locking devices stop nuts loosening from vibration: lock nut, split pin with castle nut, spring washer, Nyloc nut, tab washer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pitch of a thread is the distance between two adjacent threads. Lead is the distance moved in one turn. Single start: lead = pitch.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thread forms: V-thread (fastening), square and acme (power screws like jacks), buttress (one-way heavy loads).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Core (root) diameter is the smallest diameter of a thread. Stress in a bolt is calculated on the core area.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: A spring is an elastic part that bends under load and returns to its shape when the load is removed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of springs: helical (compression, tension), leaf (laminated), torsion, spiral (flat coil), disc (Belleville).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring index C = D / d (mean coil diameter ÷ wire diameter). Usual range 4–12.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stiffness (spring rate) k = load / deflection (N/mm).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Deflection of a close-coiled helical spring: δ = 64 W R³ n / (G d⁴) = 8 W D³ n / (G d⁴).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Springs in series: 1/k = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ (softer). Springs in parallel: k = k₁ + k₂ (stiffer).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Solid length is the length of a compression spring when coils touch each other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaf spring: longest leaf is the master leaf, with eyes at both ends. The spring is held to the axle with U-bolts and a centre bolt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring materials: high-carbon steel, silicon-manganese steel (leaf springs), chrome-vanadium steel (valve springs).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wahl's factor corrects shear stress in helical springs for wire curvature and direct shear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring surge: vibration of valve spring coils at high engine speed, so the valve does not follow the cam.
recall answer: To prevent spring surge and valve float.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bolts and springs; standard diploma textbook

key text: Welding joins metals permanently by melting and fusing them, with or without filler metal.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Butt weld: plates placed edge to edge in the same plane and welded. Fillet weld: plates at an angle (lap or T) welded at the corner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Butt weld edge preparations: square, single-V, double-V, single-U, double-U, J.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fillet weld types: transverse (load at right angles to weld) and parallel (load along the weld). Transverse is stronger.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Weld terms: leg (size s), throat (t), root, toe, face, reinforcement.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Throat thickness of a fillet weld t = 0.707 × leg size s.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strength of a parallel fillet weld P = 0.707 s l τ (per weld). Transverse: P = 0.707 s l σt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Strength of a butt weld P = t × l × σt (t = plate thickness, l = weld length).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Welding types: gas (oxy-acetylene), arc (MMAW/stick, MIG, TIG), resistance (spot, seam), and solid-state (friction).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oxy-acetylene flame is about 3200°C. Neutral flame (equal O₂ and C₂H₂) is used for most welding.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: MIG uses a consumable wire electrode with shielding gas. TIG uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Welded joints vs riveted: welded are lighter, leak-proof, faster and 100% efficient possible; but need skill and may have residual stresses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Welding defects: porosity, slag inclusion, lack of fusion, incomplete penetration, undercut, cracks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brazing and soldering join metals without melting the base metal. Soldering filler melts below 450°C; brazing above 450°C.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: Welded joints
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Welded joints; standard diploma textbook

key text: A bearing supports a moving part (usually a rotating shaft) and lets it move with little friction.
recall answer: Support a moving shaft and reduce friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Functions of a bearing: support load, guide motion, reduce friction and wear, and carry away heat.
recall answer: Support load, reduce friction (also guide motion, reduce wear).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radial (journal) bearing: load acts at right angles to the shaft axis. Thrust bearing: load acts along the shaft axis.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sliding contact bearing: the shaft slides on an oil film inside a bush (plain bearing). Rolling contact bearing: balls or rollers roll between races.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Journal bearing: the part of the shaft inside the bearing is the journal; the outer part is the bearing or bush.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of journal bearings: full journal (360°), partial journal (less than 360°), fitted bearing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydrodynamic lubrication: the rotating journal itself drags oil in and builds a pressure film that lifts the shaft.
recall answer: The rotation of the journal (wedge action).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydrostatic bearing: oil is pumped in under pressure from outside to lift the shaft, even at rest.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bearing characteristic number = Z N / p (Z = oil viscosity, N = speed, p = bearing pressure).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bearing modulus is the value of ZN/p at which friction is least. Bearings are run at about 3 times this value for safety.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat generated in a bearing Hg = μ W V (friction coefficient × load × rubbing speed).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat dissipated by a bearing depends on its surface area and the temperature difference with surrounding air.
recall answer: Bearing overheats; extra cooling is needed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rolling bearing parts: inner race, outer race, rolling elements (balls or rollers) and cage (separator).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of rolling bearings: deep groove ball, angular contact, self-aligning, cylindrical roller, taper roller, needle roller, thrust ball.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Taper roller bearings carry both radial and thrust loads. They are used in front wheel hubs and differentials.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Needle roller bearings are used in universal joints, gearbox gears and rocker arms.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engine big-end and main bearings are thin-wall split shell (plain) bearings made of steel backing with babbitt, copper-lead or aluminium-tin lining.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Properties of a good bearing material: low friction, conformability, embeddability, fatigue strength, corrosion resistance, good heat conduction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bearing crush: the shell halves stick out slightly above the housing so they are pressed tight when bolted.
recall answer: To fit tightly and prevent rotation in the housing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rolling bearings vs sliding: rolling have low starting friction and need little lubrication; sliding are cheaper, quieter and take shocks better.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bearings
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Bearings; standard diploma textbook

key text: A governor keeps engine speed nearly constant by controlling the fuel supply when load changes.
recall answer: To keep speed constant by controlling fuel supply as load changes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Governors are of two main types: centrifugal and inertia. Centrifugal governors are of two kinds: pendulum (Watt) and loaded (Porter, Proell, Hartnell, Wilson-Hartnell).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a centrifugal governor, balls fly outward as speed rises and lift the sleeve, which closes the fuel supply.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Watt governor height h = 895 / N² (h in metres, N in rpm).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Porter governor: a Watt governor with a heavy central load on the sleeve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Proell governor: like Porter but the balls are fixed on extensions of the lower arms.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hartnell governor is a spring-loaded governor with bell-crank levers. It can run at high speed and fits in a small space.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Height of governor: vertical distance from the ball centre to the point where the arms meet on the spindle axis.
recall answer: Vertical distance from ball centre to the arm-meeting point on the axis.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Equilibrium speed: the speed at which the governor balls, arms and sleeve stay at rest for a given radius.
recall answer: Speed at which the governor is in balance at a given ball radius.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mean equilibrium speed: speed at the mean ball radius. Max and min equilibrium speeds: speeds at the largest and smallest ball radius.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sleeve lift: vertical distance the sleeve travels when speed changes from minimum to maximum equilibrium speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sensitiveness = (N₂ − N₁) / N, where N is mean speed. A smaller range means a more sensitive governor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stability: a governor is stable if ball radius increases as speed increases, with one radius for each speed.
recall answer: When radius rises steadily with speed (one radius per speed).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Isochronous governor: equilibrium speed is the same at all radii. It is infinitely sensitive but in practice hunts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hunting: the governor keeps over-correcting, so speed swings above and below the mean continuously.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Effort of a governor: average force on the sleeve for a given change of speed. Power: work done at the sleeve for a given change of speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Controlling force: inward force on the balls that balances centrifugal force. A controlling force diagram tests stability.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inertia governor: works on the rate of change of speed (acceleration), so it reacts faster than a centrifugal governor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel fuel injection pumps have mechanical or electronic governors. Types: minimum-maximum speed governor and all-speed (variable speed) governor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Governors
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Governors; standard diploma textbook

key text: A flywheel is a heavy wheel on the crankshaft that stores energy during the power stroke and gives it back during other strokes.
recall answer: Store and release energy to reduce speed fluctuation within a cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flywheel vs governor: the flywheel controls speed changes within one cycle; the governor controls mean speed over many cycles when load changes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: A flywheel has no control over fuel supply. A governor has no energy storage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flywheel's other jobs in a car: carries the starter ring gear and provides the clutch friction face.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluctuation of speed = N₁ − N₂ (max − min speed in a cycle).
recall answer: Max speed − min speed in a cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of fluctuation of speed Cs = (N₁ − N₂) / N, where N = mean speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluctuation of energy ΔE = maximum energy − minimum energy in the flywheel during a cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coefficient of fluctuation of energy Ce = maximum fluctuation of energy / work done per cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Energy stored in a flywheel E = ½ I ω².
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Maximum fluctuation of energy ΔE = I ω² Cs = m k² ω² Cs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Moment of inertia I = m k² (k = radius of gyration). Rim-type flywheels put most mass at the rim.
recall answer: To get large moment of inertia with less weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turning moment (crank effort) diagram plots torque on the crankshaft against crank angle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single-cylinder and four-stroke engines need bigger flywheels than multi-cylinder engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flywheels are usually made of cast iron or cast steel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dual-mass flywheel: two parts joined by springs to absorb engine vibration before it reaches the gearbox.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flywheels
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Flywheels; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gears are toothed wheels that pass motion and power from one shaft to another without slip.
recall answer: Teeth mesh, so there is no slip.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gears for parallel shafts: spur, helical, herringbone (double helical).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Helical gears have teeth cut at an angle. They run quieter and carry more load than spur gears but produce end thrust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Herringbone (double helical) gears cancel end thrust by having two opposite helices.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gears for intersecting shafts: bevel gears (straight, spiral, zerol). Mitre gears are bevel gears with equal size at 90°.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hypoid gears: like spiral bevel but the pinion axis is offset below the crown wheel axis. Used in rear axle differentials.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hypoid gears need special extreme-pressure (EP) gear oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worm and worm wheel: for non-parallel, non-intersecting shafts at 90°. Gives very high speed reduction and is often self-locking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rack and pinion turns rotary motion into straight-line motion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pitch circle: imaginary circle on which two gears roll together without slip. Its diameter is the pitch circle diameter (PCD).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Module m = pitch circle diameter / number of teeth (D/T), in mm.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Circular pitch p = π D / T = π m. Diametral pitch P = T / D (teeth per inch).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Addendum: tooth height above the pitch circle (= 1 module). Dedendum: depth below it (= 1.25 module).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clearance = dedendum − addendum. Backlash = gap between mating teeth on the pitch circle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure angle: angle between the line of action and the common tangent to pitch circles. Standard: 20° (also 14.5°).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Involute tooth profile is most common because centre distance can vary slightly without affecting the velocity ratio.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Velocity ratio = N₁/N₂ = T₂/T₁ = D₂/D₁.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two meshing external gears turn in opposite directions. An idler gear between them makes the driven gear turn the same way as the driver.
recall answer: To change direction of rotation (without changing ratio).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Simple gear train: one gear on each shaft. Compound gear train: two or more gears on the same shaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Train value = speed of last gear / speed of first gear = product of driver teeth / product of driven teeth.
recall answer: Product of driver teeth ÷ product of driven teeth.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reverted gear train: first and last gears are on the same axis.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Epicyclic (planetary) gear train: sun gear, planet gears on a carrier, and an annulus (ring) gear. Some axes move.
recall answer: Sun gear, planet carrier (with planets), annulus (ring).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gear materials: case-hardened alloy steel for vehicle gears; cast iron for large slow gears; nylon/plastic for light quiet drives.
recall answer: Hard wear-resistant surface with tough core.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: Interference: tip of one tooth digs into the root of the mating tooth. Happens when the pinion has too few teeth.
recall answer: Too few teeth on the pinion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gears and gear trains; standard diploma textbook

key text: A boiler (steam generator) is a closed vessel that turns water into steam using heat from fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fire tube boiler: hot gases pass through tubes surrounded by water. Water tube boiler: water flows inside tubes surrounded by hot gases.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fire tube boilers: Cochran, Lancashire, Cornish, locomotive, Scotch marine. Water tube boilers: Babcock & Wilcox, Stirling, La Mont, Benson, Loeffler.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lancashire boiler has two large fire tubes (flues). Cornish boiler has one.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cochran boiler is a vertical, multi-tubular fire tube boiler. Locomotive boiler is a horizontal multi-tubular fire tube boiler.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Benson boiler is a supercritical, drum-less water tube boiler. La Mont is a forced circulation boiler.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Boiler mountings are fittings needed for safe working: safety valve, water level indicator, pressure gauge, fusible plug, steam stop valve, feed check valve, blow-off cock, manhole.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Boiler accessories improve efficiency: economiser, superheater, air preheater, feed pump, injector, steam separator.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Safety valve releases steam when pressure goes above the safe limit. Types: dead weight, lever, spring loaded, high-steam low-water.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fusible plug melts when the water level falls too low, letting steam put out the fire.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Economiser heats feed water using exhaust flue gases. Air preheater heats combustion air using flue gases.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Superheater heats saturated steam above its saturation temperature, making it dry and superheated.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Feed check valve lets water into the boiler but stops it flowing back. Blow-off cock removes sludge from the bottom.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steam engine parts: cylinder, piston, piston rod, crosshead, connecting rod, crank, slide valve, eccentric, flywheel, governor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steam engine working: the slide valve admits steam alternately to both sides of the piston (double acting), and the exhaust leaves from the other side.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steam engine is an external combustion, reciprocating engine. Its eccentric works like a small crank to move the slide valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wet steam contains water droplets. Dry saturated steam has no droplets. Dryness fraction = mass of dry steam / total mass.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Indian Boilers Act 1923 governs boiler registration and inspection in India. Boiler inspection is done by the Factories and Boilers Department.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Boilers and steam engine
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Boilers and steam engine; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ferrous metals contain iron (cast iron, steel). Non-ferrous metals do not (aluminium, copper, lead, tin, zinc).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pig iron comes from the blast furnace. Cast iron has 2–4.5% carbon. Steel has up to about 2% carbon. Wrought iron is almost pure iron.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cast iron is brittle, cheap, easy to cast, good in compression, damps vibration and wears well. It is weak in tension.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Grey cast iron: carbon as graphite flakes, grey fracture. Most common; used for engine blocks and brake drums.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: White cast iron: carbon as cementite (iron carbide). Very hard and brittle; white fracture. Used for wear parts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Malleable cast iron: made by long heat treatment (annealing) of white cast iron. It is tougher and slightly ductile.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spheroidal graphite (SG) or ductile iron: graphite as spheres, made by adding magnesium or cerium. Strong and ductile.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chilled cast iron: surface cooled fast to make it hard white iron, while the core stays grey. Used for cams and rolls.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon with carbon up to about 2% (usually less than 1.5%).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Plain carbon steels: dead mild (below 0.15% C), mild/low carbon (0.15–0.3%), medium carbon (0.3–0.6%), high carbon (0.6–1.5%).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mild steel uses: chassis frames, body panels, nuts, bolts, rivets, pipes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Medium carbon steel uses: crankshafts, axles, connecting rods, gears. High carbon steel: springs, cutting tools, files.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steel designation in India (IS): e.g. C40 means plain carbon steel with 0.40% carbon (older: 40C8).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Iron–carbon diagram phases: ferrite (soft), cementite (hard), pearlite (ferrite + cementite layers), austenite (high-temperature phase), martensite (very hard, from quenching).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Eutectoid steel has 0.8% carbon and is fully pearlite. Below 0.8% = hypo-eutectoid; above = hyper-eutectoid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Heat treatment: heating and cooling a metal in a controlled way to change its properties.
recall answer: Controlled heating and cooling to change properties of metal.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Purposes of heat treatment: relieve stresses, soften for machining, harden for wear, improve toughness, refine grain.
recall answer: Harden, soften, relieve stress, refine grain, improve toughness.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Annealing: heat steel above the critical temperature, hold, then cool very slowly in the furnace. Makes it soft and ductile.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Normalising: heat above critical temperature, then cool in still air. Gives fine grain and uniform structure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hardening: heat steel above critical temperature, then quench quickly in water or oil. Makes it very hard but brittle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tempering: reheat hardened steel to a lower temperature (below critical) and cool. Reduces brittleness, adds toughness.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Case hardening (surface hardening) makes a hard outer case with a tough core. Methods: carburising, nitriding, cyaniding, carbonitriding, flame hardening, induction hardening.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carburising adds carbon to the surface of low carbon steel at high temperature, then it is hardened.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Nitriding adds nitrogen to the surface using ammonia gas at about 500°C. No quenching is needed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cyaniding adds both carbon and nitrogen using a molten cyanide salt bath.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Induction and flame hardening heat only the surface quickly, then quench. Used for crankshaft journals and gear teeth.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alloy steel contains added elements such as nickel, chromium, manganese, molybdenum, vanadium, tungsten, silicon.
recall answer: Steel with extra alloying elements (Ni, Cr, Mo, V…).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Nickel: toughness and strength. Chromium: hardness and corrosion resistance. Manganese: strength, hardness, removes sulphur effect.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Molybdenum: strength at high temperature. Vanadium: fatigue strength and fine grain. Tungsten: hardness at red heat (tools). Silicon: springiness, magnetic properties.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stainless steel has at least 10.5% chromium (typical 18% Cr + 8% Ni, '18/8').
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: High speed steel (HSS) 18-4-1: 18% tungsten, 4% chromium, 1% vanadium. Used for cutting tools and drills.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust valve steel: silchrome (silicon-chromium) or austenitic stainless steel (21-4N). Inlet valves: plain chromium or nickel-chrome steel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Nickel-chrome-molybdenum steels are used for crankshafts, connecting rods, axle shafts and highly stressed gears.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Invar (36% nickel steel) hardly expands with heat. Used in precision instruments and some piston struts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aluminium: light (density 2.7 g/cm³, one-third of steel), conducts heat well, resists corrosion. Used for pistons, cylinder heads, alloy wheels, radiators.
recall answer: Light weight and good heat conduction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Duralumin: aluminium with about 4% copper, plus manganese and magnesium. Strong and light; used in aircraft and vehicle body parts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Y-alloy: aluminium with copper, nickel and magnesium. Keeps strength at high temperature; used for pistons and cylinder heads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brass = copper + zinc. Bronze = copper + tin. Gun metal = copper + tin + zinc.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Phosphor bronze (copper + tin + a little phosphorus) is used for bearings, bushes, worm wheels and springs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Babbitt (white metal): tin + antimony + copper (or lead base). Used for bearing linings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Solder (soft solder) = tin + lead. Used to join radiator tubes and electrical wires.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Copper: excellent conductor of heat and electricity. Used in wiring, radiator cores, starter and alternator windings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lead: heavy and soft. Used in batteries (lead-acid plates) and wheel balancing weights.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Zinc is used for galvanising — coating steel to prevent rust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Magnesium alloys are the lightest structural metals (density about 1.7 g/cm³). Used for gearbox housings and racing wheels.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Effect of sulphur in steel: red shortness (brittleness when hot). Phosphorus: cold shortness (brittle when cold).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Plastics and composites in vehicles: bumpers (polypropylene), dashboards (ABS, PVC), fuel tanks (HDPE), leaf springs and body panels (FRP).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be remoulded (PVC, polythene, nylon). Thermosetting plastics set permanently (Bakelite, epoxy).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engineering materials and heat treatment
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Engineering materials and heat treatment; standard diploma textbook

key text: The cylinder block is the main body of the engine. It holds the cylinders, coolant passages and crankcase.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single-cylinder engines (motorcycles) often have a separate cylinder barrel. Multi-cylinder engines usually have all cylinders cast in one block (monobloc).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder blocks are made of grey cast iron or aluminium alloy.
recall answer: Grey cast iron and aluminium alloy.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aluminium blocks need cast-iron or steel cylinder liners (or special coatings), because aluminium wears quickly against piston rings.
recall answer: Aluminium wears fast; liners give a hard wearing surface.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: A cylinder liner (sleeve) is a replaceable tube fitted into the cylinder bore.
recall answer: A replaceable sleeve inside the cylinder bore.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dry liner: does not touch the coolant; pressed into the block. Wet liner: touches the coolant directly; sealed with rubber rings at the bottom.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dry liners are thin (about 1.5–3 mm). Wet liners are thicker because they must withstand coolant pressure and gas pressure alone.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Liners are made of special alloy cast iron (centrifugally cast), sometimes chrome plated.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder head closes the top of the cylinders and forms the combustion chamber. It holds valves, spark plugs or injectors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder heads are made of cast iron or aluminium alloy. Aluminium heads allow higher compression without knocking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder head gasket seals the joint between block and head, keeping gas, coolant and oil apart.
recall answer: Joint between head and block (gas, coolant, oil).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Head gasket materials: copper-asbestos (older), steel-asbestos, multi-layer steel (MLS) in modern engines, composite.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Signs of a blown head gasket: white smoke, coolant loss, oil mixed with water (milky oil), overheating, bubbles in radiator.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Head bolts are tightened in a set order (from the centre outwards, spiral) and to a set torque with a torque wrench.
recall answer: From centre outwards in a spiral, to specified torque.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankcase is the lower part of the block that houses the crankshaft. The oil sump (oil pan) is bolted under it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Core plugs (frost/welch plugs) close holes left in the block from casting. They can pop out if coolant freezes.
recall answer: Seal casting holes (and give some frost protection).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Combustion chamber shapes (SI): hemispherical, wedge, bath-tub, pent-roof. Hemispherical gives best breathing and less heat loss.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder wear is greatest at the top of the ring travel, just below the ridge, and gives a taper and ovality.
recall answer: Top of ring travel (top of the bore).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reboring: worn cylinders are bored oversize and fitted with oversize pistons. Honing finishes the bore with a cross-hatch pattern.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder bore wear is measured with a cylinder bore gauge (dial bore gauge).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cylinder block, liners, head and gasket; standard diploma textbook

key text: The piston moves up and down in the cylinder. It takes the gas force and passes it to the connecting rod.
recall answer: Transmit gas force to the connecting rod.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston parts: crown (head), ring grooves and lands, skirt, and gudgeon pin bosses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pistons are usually made of aluminium alloy (light, good heat conduction). Heavy diesel engines may use cast iron or steel crowns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aluminium pistons expand more than cast iron cylinders, so they need more clearance or special designs.
recall answer: They expand more than the iron cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Split-skirt (slotted) piston: a slot in the skirt lets it expand without seizing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cam-ground piston: oval when cold, becomes round when hot. The longer axis is at right angles to the gudgeon pin.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other piston types: solid skirt, slipper (part skirt cut away), autothermic/invar-strut (steel struts control expansion), tapered.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston is tapered: smaller at the crown than the skirt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston slap: knocking noise when a worn or loose piston rocks and hits the cylinder wall, mostly when cold.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gudgeon (wrist) pin connects the piston to the connecting rod small end.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gudgeon pin types: fully floating (free in piston and rod, held by circlips), semi-floating (fixed in rod or piston), fixed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gudgeon pins are made of case-hardened steel and are often hollow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gudgeon pin is offset slightly towards the thrust side to reduce piston slap.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston rings seal the gap between piston and cylinder, control oil, and carry heat from piston to cylinder wall.
recall answer: Seal gas, control oil, transfer heat.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two types of rings: compression rings (top) and oil control (scraper) rings (bottom).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Usual petrol engine: 2 compression rings + 1 oil ring. Diesel engines may have 3–4 compression rings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil rings are slotted or have an expander so scraped oil drains back through holes in the piston.
recall answer: Through slots in the ring and holes in the piston groove.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston rings are made of fine-grained alloy cast iron; the top ring is often chrome plated.
recall answer: Alloy cast iron (top ring chrome plated).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ring end gap allows for expansion. Ring gaps are staggered around the piston (not in line).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worn rings cause blow-by, low compression, high oil consumption and blue exhaust smoke.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compression test with a compression gauge checks ring and valve sealing. A wet test (adding oil) separates ring problems from valve problems.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: The connecting rod joins the piston to the crankshaft and turns up-down motion into rotation.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Connecting rod parts: small end (gudgeon pin end, with bronze bush), shank (I-section), big end (split, with shell bearings, cap and bolts).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Connecting rods are made of drop-forged medium carbon or alloy steel; racing engines use aluminium or titanium.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Connecting rod shank has an I-section.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Small end usually has a phosphor bronze bush. Big end uses split shell (thin-wall) bearings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Some connecting rods have an oil hole (squirt hole) that sprays oil onto the cylinder wall or under the piston.
recall answer: Spray oil onto cylinder wall or piston.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft turns the reciprocating motion of pistons into rotation and carries the flywheel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft parts: main journals, crankpins, webs (cheeks), counterweights, oil holes, front end (timing gear, pulley) and rear flange (flywheel).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Counterweights on the crank webs balance the rotating weight of crankpins and connecting rods.
recall answer: To balance the crankshaft and reduce vibration.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshafts are made of drop-forged steel (carbon or alloy) or SG cast iron. Journals are hardened.
recall answer: Forged steel and SG (nodular) cast iron.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft shapes depend on cylinders: single-throw (1 cylinder), 180° two-throw, four-cylinder flat (throws at 180°), six-cylinder (throws at 120°).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Number of main bearings: a four-cylinder crankshaft usually has 3 or 5 main bearings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft end float is controlled by thrust washers or a flanged main bearing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vibration damper (harmonic balancer) on the front of the crankshaft reduces torsional vibration.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Piston, rings, connecting rod and crankshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valves open and close the inlet and exhaust ports at the right time.
recall answer: Control flow of charge in and exhaust out.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of valves: poppet (mushroom) valve, sleeve valve, rotary valve, reed valve. Poppet valves are used in almost all four-stroke engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Poppet valve parts: head, face (usually 45°, sometimes 30°), margin, stem, and grooves for the collets (keepers).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inlet valve head is larger than exhaust valve head.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust valve runs much hotter (up to about 700–800°C) than the inlet valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sodium-cooled valve: hollow exhaust valve stem partly filled with sodium. The sodium melts and carries heat from head to stem.
recall answer: To carry heat away from the valve head (cooling).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sodium melts at about 98°C, so it is liquid when the engine runs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve materials: inlet — chromium or nickel-chromium steel. Exhaust — silchrome or austenitic steel; faces often coated with stellite.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve seat inserts of hard alloy are fitted in aluminium heads.
recall answer: Aluminium is soft; inserts give a hard wearing seat.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve guide holds the valve stem in line and carries heat from the stem.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve stem seals stop oil leaking down the guide into the cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve spring closes the valve and keeps it on the seat. It is held by a spring retainer and split collets (cotters).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve float: at very high speed, the valve does not follow the cam and stays partly open.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve rotators turn the valve a little on each opening.
recall answer: Even wear and to prevent carbon deposits on seat.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve clearance (tappet clearance) is a small gap in the valve train when the valve is closed.
recall answer: To allow for expansion so valves close fully.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust valve clearance is usually more than inlet valve clearance.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Too little clearance: valve stays open, burns, and compression is lost. Too much clearance: noisy tapping and less valve lift.
recall answer: Valve does not close fully → burnt valve, low compression.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic tappets (lifters) use oil pressure to keep zero clearance automatically.
recall answer: Zero clearance automatically, quiet, no adjustment.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve arrangements: L-head (side valve), I-head (overhead valve), F-head (one over, one side), T-head (inlet and exhaust on opposite sides).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Side camshaft (OHV push-rod) mechanism: camshaft in the block → tappet (follower) → push rod → rocker arm → valve.
recall answer: Cam → tappet → push rod → rocker arm → valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overhead camshaft (OHC): the camshaft is in the cylinder head and works the valves directly or through rockers/followers.
recall answer: Fewer parts, less inertia, higher rpm.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: SOHC: single overhead camshaft. DOHC: two overhead camshafts, one for inlet and one for exhaust valves.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Multi-valve engines (3, 4 or 5 valves per cylinder) breathe better and allow a central spark plug.
recall answer: Better breathing, more power, central plug.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camshaft opens the valves at the right time. It has one cam (lobe) for each valve and runs at half crankshaft speed in four-stroke engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cam terms: base circle, nose (tip), flank, lift, ramp.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camshafts may also drive the distributor, oil pump and mechanical fuel pump (via an eccentric).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camshaft drives: gear drive, chain drive (timing chain with tensioner), belt drive (toothed timing belt).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Timing belts are quiet and light but must be replaced at set intervals. Chains last longer but are noisier.
recall answer: Needs periodic replacement; failure can damage valves.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Timing marks on crank and cam sprockets must line up when fitting the chain or belt.
recall answer: Timing marks on crank and cam sprockets.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camshafts are made of cast iron (chilled or hardenable) or forged steel; cam lobes are hardened.
recall answer: Chilled cast iron or forged steel (hardened lobes).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cam followers: flat (mushroom), roller, knife-edge, spherical. Roller followers reduce friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valve grinding (lapping) with grinding paste makes the valve face and seat seal perfectly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Valves, valve mechanisms and camshaft; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol fuel system parts: tank, fuel lines, filter, fuel pump, carburettor or injectors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel feed systems: gravity feed, pressure feed, vacuum feed, pump feed (mechanical or electrical).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: AC mechanical fuel pump: a diaphragm pump worked by a rocker arm from an eccentric on the camshaft.
recall answer: Eccentric on the camshaft (via rocker arm).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: AC pump parts: diaphragm, rocker arm, return spring, inlet and outlet valves, filter screen, priming lever.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: In the AC pump, the spring pushes fuel out. When the float bowl is full, the diaphragm stays down and the pump idles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: SU electrical fuel pump: a solenoid pulls a diaphragm; contact points switch it off and on.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electric pumps can be fitted near the tank, away from engine heat.
recall answer: Fitted away from heat; fuel at once on switch-on; less vapour lock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Modern fuel-injected cars use an electric in-tank (submerged) roller-cell or turbine pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vapour lock: petrol boils in hot fuel lines and vapour blocks fuel flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol filters remove dirt and water. Types: in-line paper filter, sediment bowl, gauze strainer in tank and pump.
recall answer: To remove dirt and water from fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air cleaner removes dust from air entering the engine. It also silences intake noise and acts as a flame arrester.
recall answer: Filter dust, reduce intake noise (and arrest backfire flame).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air cleaner types: dry (paper element), wet (oil-wetted mesh), oil bath. Paper dry type is most common in cars.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centrifugal (cyclone) pre-cleaners are used on trucks and tractors in dusty conditions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: A choked air filter makes the mixture rich, raises fuel consumption and causes black smoke.
recall answer: Rich mixture, high fuel consumption, black smoke.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Petrol fuel feed, filters and air cleaners; standard diploma textbook

key text: A carburettor mixes petrol with air in the correct ratio and supplies it to the engine as a fine spray.
recall answer: Mix air and petrol in correct proportion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carburettor works on the venturi (Bernoulli) principle: air speeds up in the narrow venturi, pressure drops, and petrol is sucked from the jet.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Simple carburettor parts: float chamber with float and needle valve, main jet, discharge nozzle, venturi, throttle valve, choke valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Throttle valve (butterfly) controls the amount of mixture entering the engine and so controls speed and power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: The fuel nozzle tip is slightly above the fuel level in the float chamber.
recall answer: To stop fuel overflowing when the engine is off.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: A simple carburettor gives a richer mixture as speed rises.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compensation devices keep mixture correct at all speeds: air bleed jet, compensating jet, emulsion tube, auxiliary air valve, back suction control.
recall answer: Air bleed jet (or compensating jet, emulsion tube).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chemically correct air-fuel ratio: about 15:1. Rich mixture: less air (e.g. 12:1). Lean (weak) mixture: more air (e.g. 17:1).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mixture requirements: cold starting very rich (up to 5:1 or 9:1), idling rich (about 12:1), cruising lean (about 16–17:1), full power/acceleration rich (about 12–13:1).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Best economy mixture is slightly lean (about 16:1). Best power mixture is slightly rich (about 12.5:1).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Modern carburettor circuits: float system, starting (choke) system, idle and slow-speed system, main metering (high speed) system, acceleration pump system, power (economiser) system.
recall answer: Float, choke, idle, main metering, accelerating pump, power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Idle and slow-speed system supplies fuel through an idle port below the closed throttle, where vacuum is high.
recall answer: Idle port below the throttle valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Idle mixture screw adjusts idle mixture; idle speed (throttle stop) screw adjusts idle rpm.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transfer (progression) ports just above the closed throttle feed extra fuel as the throttle starts to open.
recall answer: Smooth change from idle to main circuit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Main metering (high speed) system supplies fuel through the main jet and nozzle at cruising and higher speeds.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Acceleration pump squirts extra fuel when the throttle is opened suddenly.
recall answer: Prevent hesitation (lean mixture) on sudden throttle opening.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Power (economiser) system gives extra fuel at full throttle, opened by low vacuum or a mechanical link.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Choke valve is a butterfly above the venturi. Closing it gives a very rich mixture for cold starting.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Automatic choke uses a bimetallic spring heated by the engine to open the choke as the engine warms.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant vacuum (CV) carburettor: venturi size changes with a piston/slide lifted by vacuum (SU, Stromberg).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fixed venturi (constant choke) carburettors: Solex, Zenith, Carter. Variable venturi (constant vacuum): SU, Stromberg.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Down-draught, up-draught and side-draught carburettors are named by air flow direction. Down-draught is common in cars.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Multi-barrel carburettors have two or four throats; the secondary barrels open only at high load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carburettor faults: flooding (stuck needle valve), lean mixture (blocked jet), rich mixture (choke stuck, high float level), icing.
recall answer: Needle valve stuck open / float punctured.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carburettor icing: fuel evaporation cools the venturi so much that moisture freezes on it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carburettors
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Carburettors; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inlet (intake) manifold carries air or air–fuel mixture from the carburettor or throttle body to each cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inlet manifolds are made of cast aluminium or plastic (nylon composite) in modern engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hot spot: part of the inlet manifold heated by exhaust or coolant to help petrol vaporise in carburettor engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inlet manifold types: single plane, dual plane, log type, individual runners (tuned).
recall answer: Single plane, dual plane, log, tuned runners.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Long intake runners give better low-speed torque; short runners give better high-speed power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Variable intake system (VIS) switches between long and short runners with valves controlled by the ECU.
recall answer: Change runner length for good torque and power at all speeds.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: VVT (variable valve timing) changes when the valves open and close depending on engine speed and load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: VVT is usually done by a cam phaser on the camshaft sprocket, moved by oil pressure controlled by an ECU solenoid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: CVVT (continuously variable valve timing) can set any timing within its range, not just two fixed positions.
recall answer: CVVT adjusts timing continuously, not in steps.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brand names: Honda VTEC (also changes lift), Toyota VVT-i, Hyundai CVVT, Maruti VVT.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Benefits of VVT: more torque at low rpm, more power at high rpm, better fuel economy, smoother idle, lower emissions (internal EGR).
recall answer: More power and torque, better economy, lower emissions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust manifold collects burnt gases from all cylinders and sends them to the exhaust pipe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust manifolds are made of cast iron or stainless steel tubes (headers).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tuned exhaust headers (e.g. 4-into-1, 4-2-1) use pressure waves to help pull exhaust out (scavenging).
recall answer: Better scavenging, less back pressure, more power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust system parts: exhaust manifold, front pipe, catalytic converter, resonator, muffler (silencer), tail pipe.
recall answer: Manifold → catalytic converter → muffler → tail pipe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Catalytic converter changes harmful gases (CO, HC, NOx) into less harmful CO₂, H₂O and N₂ using catalysts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Catalysts used: platinum and palladium (oxidise CO and HC), rhodium (reduces NOx). Coated on a ceramic honeycomb.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-way converter: oxidises CO and HC only. Three-way converter: also reduces NOx, needs mixture near 14.7:1 (controlled by lambda sensor).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Catalytic converter works only when hot (light-off temperature about 250–300°C).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaded petrol destroys catalytic converters (lead poisoning of the catalyst).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel engines use a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC), diesel particulate filter (DPF) and SCR with urea (AdBlue) for NOx.
