source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Muffler (silencer) reduces exhaust noise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Muffler types: baffle type, wave cancellation (Helmholtz/resonator), absorption (straight-through with glass wool), combined.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wave cancellation muffler splits gas into two paths of different lengths so sound waves meet out of phase and cancel.
recall answer: Sound waves meet out of phase and cancel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Back pressure: resistance to exhaust flow. Too much back pressure reduces power and raises fuel consumption.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Removing or modifying silencers is an offence. Noise limits are set under the Central Motor Vehicles Rules.
recall answer: No — it is an offence (noise limits under CMVR).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Manifolds, VVT, catalytic converter and muffler; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel fuel system order: tank → feed (lift) pump → primary filter → secondary filter → injection pump → high-pressure pipes → injectors. Leak-off returns to tank.
recall answer: Tank, feed pump, filters, injection pump, injectors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel feed (lift / transfer) pump sends fuel from the tank to the injection pump at low pressure (about 1–2 bar).
recall answer: Supply fuel from tank to injection pump at low pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hand priming pump on the feed pump is used to fill the system and bleed out air after filter change.
recall answer: To fill the fuel system and bleed air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air lock in diesel lines prevents injection; the system is bled at filter and pump bleed screws.
recall answer: Bleed the fuel system to remove air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel filters: primary (coarse, often with water separator) and secondary (fine, paper element).
recall answer: Injection pump and injectors have very fine clearances.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Water separator (sedimenter) collects water at the bottom of the filter bowl; it must be drained regularly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel injection pump (FIP) supplies exact, metered fuel at very high pressure to each injector at the right time.
recall answer: Meter and pressurise fuel, deliver at right time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of injection pumps: in-line (jerk) pump with one element per cylinder, distributor (rotary) pump with one element for all cylinders, unit injector, and common rail.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: In-line (Bosch) pump: each element has a plunger with a helix; rotating the plunger with a control rack changes fuel quantity.
recall answer: Rotating the plunger (helix) via control rack.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Delivery valve in each pump element stops back-flow and gives sharp end of injection (prevents dribbling).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor (rotary) type pump (e.g. Bosch VE, CAV DPA): one pumping element and a rotor distribute fuel to all cylinders in turn.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor pumps suit small, high-speed diesel engines in cars and light vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor pumps are lubricated by diesel itself, so diesel quality (lubricity) matters.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel injector (nozzle) sprays diesel as a fine mist into the cylinder.
recall answer: Atomise and spray fuel into the cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mechanical injector: a spring holds the needle closed; fuel pressure lifts it at the opening pressure (about 150–250 bar in older engines).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Nozzle types: single-hole, multi-hole (direct injection), pintle and pintaux (indirect injection).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Injector testing checks opening pressure, spray pattern, leakage and chatter on an injector tester.
recall answer: Opening pressure, spray pattern, leak-back, chatter.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leak-off pipes return extra fuel (used to lubricate and cool the injector needle) to the tank.
recall answer: Return excess fuel to the tank.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Unit injector combines the pump and injector in one unit at each cylinder, driven by a camshaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel injection timing is advanced at higher speeds by an automatic timer (advance unit) in the pump.
recall answer: Automatic timing (advance) device in the pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel smoke colours: black = too much fuel or too little air; blue = oil burning; white = unburnt fuel (cold, retarded timing) or water.
recall answer: Over-fuelling or not enough air (choked filter, bad injector).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbocharger uses exhaust gas to spin a turbine, which drives a compressor that forces more air into the engine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbocharger parts: turbine wheel (exhaust side), compressor wheel (intake side), common shaft, centre bearing housing (oil-lubricated), wastegate.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbochargers spin very fast (up to about 1–2 lakh rpm) and are lubricated by engine oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Let a turbo engine idle for a short time before switching off.
recall answer: To let the turbo slow down and cool with oil flowing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wastegate is a valve that lets some exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Intercooler (charge air cooler) cools the compressed air from the turbo before it enters the engine.
recall answer: Cool compressed air to make it denser.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbo lag is the delay between pressing the accelerator and the turbo giving boost.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbo lag is reduced by small/light turbines, twin-scroll or twin turbos, ball-bearing turbos and variable geometry turbos (VGT).
recall answer: VGT, twin-scroll, smaller turbo, twin turbos.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Variable geometry turbocharger (VGT/VNT) has movable vanes around the turbine that change the gas flow angle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turbocharger types: single, twin (parallel or sequential), twin-scroll, VGT, electric-assisted.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Supercharger vs turbocharger: supercharger is belt-driven by the engine (no lag, uses engine power); turbo uses waste exhaust (efficient, but lag).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel fuel system and turbocharger
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Diesel fuel system and turbocharger; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engine lubrication reduces friction and wear, cools parts, seals piston rings, cleans and protects from rust.
recall answer: Reduce friction, cool, seal, clean, prevent rust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lubrication systems: petroil (two-stroke), splash, pressure feed (forced), semi-pressure (combined), dry sump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Splash lubrication: dippers on the connecting rod big ends dip into oil troughs and splash oil around.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure feed: oil pump sends oil through a filter and main gallery to main bearings, big ends (via drilled crankshaft), camshaft bearings and valve gear.
recall answer: Through drilled passages in the crankshaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wet sump: oil is stored in the sump under the crankcase. Most cars use wet sump.
recall answer: In the sump under the crankcase.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dry sump: oil is pumped out of the sump by a scavenge pump to a separate tank, and a pressure pump feeds the engine from it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dry sump is used in racing cars, aircraft, some motorcycles and off-road vehicles.
recall answer: Racing cars, aircraft, some bikes and off-road vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil pump types: gear pump (external gears), rotor (gerotor) pump, vane pump, plunger pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rotor (gerotor) pump: an inner rotor with one lobe less than the outer rotor turns inside it, trapping and pushing oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil strainer (pick-up screen) at the pump inlet stops large particles entering the pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure relief valve limits maximum oil pressure by returning excess oil to the sump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil pressure indicator: a warning light (pressure switch) or gauge on the dashboard. The light comes on when pressure is too low.
recall answer: Stop the engine at once and check oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil filtration systems: full-flow (all oil passes the filter before bearings) and bypass (only part of the oil is filtered).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Full-flow filters have a bypass valve that opens if the filter gets blocked.
recall answer: To keep oil flowing if the filter clogs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil filter types: cartridge (replaceable element) and spin-on (throw-away). Elements: paper, cloth, felt; centrifugal filters in some diesels.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil cooler: a small radiator for engine oil, cooled by air or coolant.
recall answer: Keep oil temperature in safe range.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil seals (lip seals) stop oil leaking where shafts come out of the engine, e.g. front and rear crankshaft seals.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankcase ventilation removes blow-by gases (unburnt fuel, water vapour, acids) from the crankcase.
recall answer: Remove blow-by gases that contaminate oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Old open (road draught) ventilation vented gases to air. Modern PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) sends them into the intake to be burnt.
recall answer: Into the intake manifold to be burnt.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil level is checked with the dipstick, engine off and on level ground. Keep it between MIN and MAX marks.
recall answer: With the dipstick, on level ground, engine off.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil grades: SAE (viscosity, e.g. 15W-40), API service (S for petrol, C for diesel, e.g. API SN, CK-4).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oil additives: detergent-dispersants, anti-wear (ZDDP), anti-oxidants, viscosity index improvers, pour point depressants, anti-foam, corrosion inhibitors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Low oil pressure causes: low oil level, worn bearings, worn pump, blocked strainer, thin oil, stuck relief valve.
recall answer: Low oil level, worn bearings or pump, thin oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lubrication system
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Lubrication system; standard diploma textbook

key text: The cooling system removes extra heat from the engine and keeps it at the best working temperature (about 80–95°C).
recall answer: Remove excess heat and keep correct temperature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: About 30% of fuel heat is removed by the cooling system.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two types of cooling: air cooling and water (liquid) cooling.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air cooling uses fins on the cylinder and head to give off heat to air. Fans and cowls (shrouds) help in scooters and some engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air cooling: light, simple, no leaks or freezing; but noisy, uneven cooling and limited to small engines.
recall answer: Uneven cooling / noisy / only for small engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Water cooling parts: water jackets, water pump, radiator, pressure cap, thermostat, fan, hoses, coolant reservoir.
recall answer: Jackets, pump, radiator, cap, thermostat, fan, hoses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermo-syphon cooling: water circulates by itself because hot water rises and cool water sinks. No pump is used.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermo-syphon is slow; the radiator must be above the engine and water level kept high. Used in old and small stationary engines.
recall answer: Slow circulation; radiator must be high; level critical.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pump circulation (forced) system: a centrifugal water pump driven by belt circulates coolant quickly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Water pump is driven by the fan belt or timing belt from the crankshaft. It has an impeller, seal and bearing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermostat is a valve between engine and radiator. It stays closed when cold and opens at about 80–90°C.
recall answer: Quick warm-up and control engine temperature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermostat types: wax pellet (most common), bellows (with volatile liquid like alcohol), bimetallic.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermostat stuck closed → overheating. Stuck open → engine runs cold, heater weak, more fuel use.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bypass passage lets coolant circulate within the engine while the thermostat is closed.
recall answer: Circulate coolant in engine when thermostat is closed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radiator is a heat exchanger that cools hot coolant using air flowing through its core.
recall answer: Transfer heat from coolant to air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radiator parts: upper tank (inlet), core, lower tank (outlet), filler neck with pressure cap, drain cock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radiator core types: tubular (fin and tube) and cellular (honeycomb). Flow types: down-flow and cross-flow.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radiators are made of copper-brass (older) or aluminium core with plastic tanks (modern).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure cap raises the system pressure (about 0.9–1.1 bar extra), which raises the boiling point of coolant to about 120°C.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressure cap has two valves: a pressure valve (opens to the overflow when pressure is high) and a vacuum valve (lets coolant back in when cooling down).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never open a hot radiator cap.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coolant = water + antifreeze (ethylene glycol or propylene glycol) + corrosion inhibitors. Usually 50:50 mix.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Antifreeze is used even in hot places like Kerala because it prevents rust and scale and raises boiling point.
recall answer: Corrosion protection and higher boiling point.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other antifreeze materials: methanol, ethanol (wood alcohol, alcohol), glycerine. Ethylene glycol is preferred.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Expansion (overflow) tank stores coolant pushed out when hot and returns it when cold.
recall answer: Store expanding coolant and return it when cool.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cooling fan types: belt-driven fixed fan, viscous (fluid) coupling fan, thermostatically controlled electric fan.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Viscous fan coupling uses silicone fluid; it slips when cool and locks up when the air behind the radiator is hot.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fan shroud directs air through the whole radiator core.
recall answer: Direct air through the radiator core.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overheating causes: low coolant, leaks, loose or broken fan belt, stuck thermostat, blocked radiator, faulty pump, fan failure, head gasket leak.
recall answer: Low coolant, broken belt, stuck thermostat, blocked radiator, fan failure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Temperature gauge sender is a thermistor in the coolant passage; resistance falls as temperature rises.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cooling system
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Cooling system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chassis means the whole vehicle without the body: frame, engine, transmission, suspension, steering, brakes and wheels.
recall answer: The vehicle without its body (frame + running gear).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: The frame is the backbone of the chassis. It supports the body, engine and all other units.
recall answer: Support all parts and carry loads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Loads on a frame: weight of vehicle and passengers (bending), road twisting (torsion), braking and acceleration (longitudinal), cornering (side), and impacts.
recall answer: Bending, torsion, braking, side and impact loads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Conventional (ladder) frame: two long side members joined by cross members, like a ladder. Used in trucks, buses and SUVs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frameless (integral / unitary / monocoque) construction: body and frame are one welded shell. Used in most cars.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Semi-integral frame: a light frame is joined to the body through rubber mounts, sharing some loads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other frame types: backbone (central tube), X-frame, perimeter frame, space frame (tube cage, racing cars).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frame sections used for side members: channel (C) section (most common), box section, tubular section, I-section.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Box section is best against torsion (twisting). Channel section is best in bending for its weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frame side members are deeper in the middle (between axles) where bending moment is greatest.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frame is narrow at the front (kick-up / narrowed) to allow wheels to turn for steering, and upswept at the rear over the axle.
recall answer: To give room for rear axle movement.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frame material: mild steel or low-alloy steel sheet, pressed and riveted or welded. Some cars use aluminium.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sub-frame: a smaller separate frame carrying the engine, suspension or axle, bolted to the main body through rubber mounts.
recall answer: A small frame carrying engine/suspension, mounted to the body.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bumpers absorb small impacts and protect the body. Modern bumpers are plastic covers over energy-absorbing foam and a steel or aluminium beam.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fitting bull bars (crash guards) on cars is banned in India.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crumple zones: front and rear parts of the body designed to crush in a crash, absorbing energy. The passenger cell stays rigid.
recall answer: Absorb crash energy so the cabin stays safe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Frame defects: cracks, bending, sagging, twisting and loose rivets. Alignment is checked with diagonal measurements.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chassis layouts: front engine rear drive, front engine front drive, rear engine rear drive, mid engine, four-wheel drive.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chassis and frame
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Chassis and frame; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dead axle carries only weight; it does not drive the wheels. Live axle carries weight and also drives the wheels.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front axle of a rear-wheel-drive vehicle is a dead axle. Front axle of a front-wheel-drive vehicle is a live axle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front axle beam has an I-section in the middle and round or elliptical section near the ends.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front axle beam is dropped (bent down) in the middle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front axle is made of drop-forged medium carbon steel or nickel steel.
recall answer: Drop-forged medium carbon or alloy steel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stub axle carries the front wheel and turns on a kingpin for steering.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stub axle types: Elliott, reversed Elliott, Lemoine, reversed Lemoine.
recall answer: Elliott, reversed Elliott, Lemoine, reversed Lemoine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Elliott type: the axle beam end fits between the forked (yoke) stub axle. Reversed Elliott: the beam end is forked and the stub axle fits inside.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lemoine type: an L-shaped stub axle fits under the beam end (no fork). Reversed Lemoine fits above.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kingpin (swivel pin) joins the stub axle to the axle beam and lets it swing for steering.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Modern cars with independent suspension use ball joints instead of kingpins.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thrust bearing between the stub axle and the beam carries the vehicle weight while letting the stub axle turn.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering knuckle is the part carrying the stub axle, steering arm and brake parts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front axle and stub axle
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Front axle and stub axle; standard diploma textbook

key text: Suspension connects wheels to the frame and absorbs road shocks.
recall answer: Absorb road shocks and keep wheels on road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Functions of suspension: comfort, road holding, stability on turns and braking, protect load and parts, carry weight.
recall answer: Comfort, road holding, stability, carry load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sprung weight: parts supported by springs (body, frame, engine). Unsprung weight: parts not supported by springs (wheels, tyres, axles, brakes).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rigid axle (dependent) suspension: both wheels are on one axle, so a bump on one wheel affects the other.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Independent suspension: each wheel moves up and down separately.
recall answer: One wheel's bump does not affect the other; better ride.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Independent front suspension types: MacPherson strut, double wishbone, trailing link, swinging axle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: MacPherson strut: a shock absorber and coil spring in one unit, which also acts as the steering pivot, with one lower arm.
recall answer: The strut itself (top mount and lower ball joint).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Double wishbone: upper and lower A-shaped arms hold the wheel. Gives good control of camber.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-wheeler front suspension: telescopic fork (most common), leading link, trailing link. Rear: swing arm with twin shocks or mono-shock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Three-wheeler (autorickshaw) front: single trailing/leading link with coil spring or torsion bar and shock absorber. Rear: swing arms with coil springs.
recall answer: Single link (trailing/leading) with spring and shock absorber.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rear suspension types: rigid axle with leaf springs (trucks, buses), rigid axle with coil springs and links, twist beam (small FWD cars), independent multi-link.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring types used: leaf (laminated), coil, torsion bar, rubber, air (pneumatic), hydro-pneumatic.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaf spring types: semi-elliptic (most common), quarter-elliptic, three-quarter elliptic, full elliptic, transverse.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaf spring parts: master leaf with eyes, other leaves, centre bolt, rebound clips, U-bolts, spring seat, shackle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaves are of graded length so the spring has nearly uniform strength along its length.
recall answer: To give uniform strength (more leaves at centre).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaf springs also locate the axle and transmit driving and braking forces (Hotchkiss drive).
recall answer: Locate the axle and carry drive/brake forces.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Interleaf friction in a leaf spring damps vibration, but makes the ride harsher. Leaves are greased or have plastic inserts.
recall answer: To reduce interleaf friction and noise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring shackle: a swinging link at one end of the leaf spring that allows the spring length to change as it flexes.
recall answer: To allow change in spring length during flexing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shackle pin connects the shackle to the spring eye and frame. Eyes have bushes (bronze or rubber).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front end of a leaf spring is usually fixed to the frame by a bracket; the rear end has the shackle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Helper spring: an extra small leaf spring above the main spring that works only under heavy load.
recall answer: An extra spring that acts only under heavy load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coil springs: light, compact, need no lubrication, but cannot locate the axle, so links or arms are needed.
recall answer: Cannot locate axle/carry side or drive forces; need links.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coil spring arrangements: around the shock absorber (coil-over), between lower arm and body, on rigid axle with links (four-link, Panhard rod).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air suspension uses rubber air bags (bellows) with compressed air. A levelling valve keeps ride height constant with load.
recall answer: Constant height and soft ride at any load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Anti-roll bar (stabiliser bar) links left and right suspension to reduce body roll on turns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: A shock absorber (damper) controls spring oscillations. It turns movement energy into heat in oil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Springs absorb shocks; shock absorbers do not absorb shocks — they damp (calm) the spring movement.
recall answer: No — springs absorb, dampers control the bounce.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Telescopic shock absorber: piston with small valves moves in an oil-filled cylinder. Oil forced through valves resists motion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Telescopic damper parts: inner pressure tube, outer reservoir tube, piston with valves, piston rod, foot (base) valve, seal and dust cover.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Shock absorbers usually resist more on rebound (extension) than on bump (compression).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single-acting damper works only on rebound. Double-acting works on both bump and rebound. Most are double-acting.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gas-charged (monotube) shock absorbers have nitrogen gas under pressure to stop oil foaming (aeration).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other damper types: lever arm (older), friction (old), adjustable and electronically controlled (adaptive) dampers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worn shock absorbers: car keeps bouncing, nose dives on braking, poor grip, uneven (cupped) tyre wear, oil leaks.
recall answer: Bounce test: push down and see if it bounces more than once or twice.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rubber bump stops (bumpers) prevent metal-to-metal contact at full suspension travel.
recall answer: Prevent metal contact at full compression.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Suspension, springs and shock absorbers
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Suspension, springs and shock absorbers; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering system lets the driver turn the front wheels to change direction.
recall answer: Turn the wheels to control direction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Requirements of steering: easy to turn, self-centring after a turn, stable straight running, little road shock to the wheel, correct turning geometry.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: For true rolling on a turn, all wheels must turn about one common centre (instantaneous centre).
recall answer: All wheels turn about a common centre.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: On a turn, the inner front wheel turns more sharply than the outer wheel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Condition for correct steering: cot φ − cot θ = c / b. (φ outer angle, θ inner angle, c = distance between kingpin centres, b = wheelbase).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ackermann steering mechanism uses a trapezium linkage (steering arms angled inward) and has only turning pairs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ackermann gives correct steering in only three positions: straight ahead and one position each to left and right.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Davis steering gear uses sliding pairs and gives correct steering in all positions. It is not used much because sliding parts wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ackermann has turning pairs only; Davis has sliding pairs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fifth wheel steering: the whole front axle turns about a central pivot. Used in horse carts and trailers (fifth wheel coupling).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering linkage parts (rigid axle): steering wheel → column → gearbox → drop arm (pitman arm) → drag link → steering arm → stub axle; track rod joins both stub axles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Drop arm (pitman arm) is attached to the steering gearbox output shaft; it swings and moves the drag link.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tie rod ends and drag link ends use ball joints so they can move in all directions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Independent front suspension uses a divided (split) track rod with an idler arm or rack and pinion.
recall answer: So each wheel can move up and down without bump steer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering gearbox reduces the effort needed and changes the direction of motion. Steering gear ratio is usually 12:1 to 24:1.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering gearbox types: worm and sector, worm and roller, worm and nut, recirculating ball, cam and lever, rack and pinion.
recall answer: Worm & sector, worm & roller, recirculating ball, rack & pinion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worm and sector: a worm on the column turns a toothed sector on the drop arm shaft.
recall answer: A toothed sector (part of a gear).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worm and roller: a roller on the sector shaft engages an hourglass worm, giving rolling contact and less friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Recirculating ball: steel balls roll between the worm and a nut; the nut moves a sector. Very low friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rack and pinion: a pinion on the steering column moves a toothed rack sideways, which moves the tie rods.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reversible steering: road shocks are felt at the steering wheel. Irreversible: road shocks are not passed back. Most are semi-reversible.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Power steering uses hydraulic or electric power to reduce the driver's effort.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic power steering parts: engine-driven pump (vane type), reservoir, control valve, power cylinder, hoses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Integral power steering: control valve and power cylinder are built into the steering gearbox.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Linkage type power steering: control valve and power cylinder are separate and act on the steering linkage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electric power steering (EPS) uses an electric motor on the column or rack, controlled by a torque sensor and ECU.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Power steering is fail-safe: if power fails, the driver can still steer manually with more effort.
recall answer: Yes, manually but with more effort.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Collapsible steering column collapses on impact to protect the driver's chest. Types: mesh/lattice, telescopic (sliding), shear capsule, convoluted tube.
recall answer: Collapse in a crash to protect the driver.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheel alignment angles: camber, caster, kingpin inclination (KPI / SAI), toe-in/toe-out, toe-out on turns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camber: tilt of the wheel inward or outward at the top, seen from the front. Positive camber: top tilts out.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Excess camber causes tyre wear on one shoulder (positive camber wears the outer edge) and pulling to one side.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Caster: backward tilt of the kingpin/steering axis seen from the side. Positive caster: top tilts towards the rear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Too much caster makes steering heavy; too little makes the vehicle wander. Unequal caster makes it pull to one side.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kingpin inclination (KPI / steering axis inclination): inward tilt of the kingpin at the top, seen from the front. Usually 7–8°.
recall answer: Reduce steering effort and give self-centring.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Scrub radius (offset): distance on the road between the tyre centre and the point where the steering axis meets the ground.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Toe-in: front of wheels closer than the rear (seen from above). Toe-out: front further apart. Usually 2–4 mm toe-in for RWD.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front-wheel-drive cars often have zero or slight toe-out.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wrong toe causes feather-edge (saw-tooth) tyre wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Toe-out on turns: on a turn the inner wheel turns more than the outer, giving toe-out. Provided by the Ackermann layout.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Factors affecting wheel alignment: worn kingpins, ball joints and tie rod ends, bent parts, sagging springs, wrong tyre pressure, accidents, potholes.
recall answer: Worn joints, bent parts, weak springs, accidents, tyre pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering geometry faults: wheel wobble/shimmy, wander, pull to one side, hard steering, poor return after turns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Turning radius: radius of the circle traced by the outer front wheel at full lock. Smaller is more manoeuvrable.
recall answer: Outer front wheel at full lock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Over-steer: vehicle turns more than the driver wants (rear slides out). Under-steer: turns less (front pushes wide).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Steering system and wheel alignment
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Steering system and wheel alignment; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brakes slow down or stop a vehicle by turning its kinetic energy into heat through friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Classification of brakes: by purpose (service, parking), by location (wheel, transmission), by construction (drum, disc), by actuation (mechanical, hydraulic, air, vacuum servo, electric).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Service brake (foot brake) is used during driving. Parking brake (hand brake) holds the parked vehicle and is usually mechanical on rear wheels.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mechanical brakes use rods, cables and levers to push the brake shoes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Drum brake: shoes press outward against a rotating drum (internal expanding).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Internal expanding brake: shoes inside the drum expand outward. External contracting brake: a band outside the drum tightens around it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Drum brake parts: back plate, two shoes with linings, wheel cylinder or cam, retracting springs, anchor pin, adjuster, drum.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leading shoe: drum rotation helps press it harder (self-energising). Trailing shoe: drum rotation pushes it away.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake shoes are made of pressed steel or cast iron, lined with friction material (riveted or bonded).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake lining materials: asbestos-free organic, semi-metallic, ceramic, sintered metal. Asbestos is banned due to health risk.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake fade: loss of braking when brakes get very hot from repeated use, for example on long downhill roads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Use engine braking (lower gear) on long descents to avoid brake fade.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Disc brake: a disc (rotor) turns with the wheel; a caliper squeezes friction pads on both sides of it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Disc brake advantages: better cooling, less fade, self-cleaning (throws off water), easy pad change, even braking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Disc brakes are not self-energising, so they need more pedal force; a brake booster is usually fitted.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Caliper types: fixed caliper (pistons on both sides) and floating/sliding caliper (piston on one side; caliper slides).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ventilated discs have air passages between two faces for better cooling. Discs are made of grey cast iron.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic brakes work on Pascal's law: pedal force builds pressure in the master cylinder, which is passed equally to all wheel cylinders.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic brake parts: brake pedal, master cylinder, reservoir, brake lines (pipes and hoses), wheel cylinders or calipers, brake fluid.
recall answer: Pedal, master cylinder, lines, wheel cylinders/calipers, fluid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Master cylinder converts pedal force into hydraulic pressure. Parts: reservoir, piston, primary and secondary cups, return spring, check valve, compensating port, inlet port.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compensating port lets fluid flow between reservoir and cylinder when brakes are off, making up for expansion, contraction and lining wear.
recall answer: Allow fluid to expand/return to reservoir; compensate wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Check valve in a master cylinder keeps a small residual pressure in the lines (in drum systems).
recall answer: To keep cups sealed and prevent air entry.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tandem master cylinder has two pistons one behind the other, feeding two separate circuits (dual circuit).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dual circuit splits: front/rear (vertical split) or diagonal (each circuit has one front and the opposite rear wheel).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheel cylinder: fluid pressure pushes its two pistons outward to expand the brake shoes against the drum.
recall answer: Push brake shoes outward using fluid pressure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheel cylinder types: double-piston (both shoes), single-piston (one shoe), stepped (different piston sizes).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake bleeding removes air from hydraulic brake lines.
recall answer: To remove air from the system.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bleeding is done at each wheel's bleed screw, usually starting from the wheel farthest from the master cylinder.
recall answer: The one farthest from the master cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spongy pedal: air in the lines. Pedal goes to floor slowly: leaking cups. Hard pedal: booster failure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Servo (power-assisted) brake uses an outside power source to add to the driver's pedal force.
recall answer: Brake assisted by vacuum, air or hydraulic power.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Servo brake types: vacuum servo (most cars), air servo, hydraulic servo, mechanical self-servo (leading shoe).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vacuum booster: a large diaphragm with engine vacuum on both sides. Pressing the pedal lets air into one side; the pressure difference pushes the master cylinder.
recall answer: Air on one side, vacuum on the other pushes the diaphragm to help the pedal.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel engines have little manifold vacuum, so they use an engine-driven vacuum pump (exhauster) for the booster.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Suspended vacuum type: vacuum on both sides of the diaphragm at rest. Atmospheric suspended: air on both sides at rest. Most boosters are vacuum-suspended.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air (pneumatic) brakes use compressed air to apply the brakes. Used in heavy vehicles like trucks and buses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air brake parts: compressor, governor/unloader, air dryer, reservoir (tanks), foot (brake) valve, brake chambers, slack adjusters, S-cam, relay and quick release valves, pressure gauge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air brake working: compressor fills reservoirs (about 7–8 bar). Pressing the foot valve sends air to brake chambers, whose push rods turn the slack adjuster and S-cam, spreading the shoes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake chamber converts air pressure into mechanical force using a diaphragm and push rod.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Slack adjuster joins the brake chamber push rod to the S-cam shaft and adjusts for lining wear.
recall answer: Link push rod to cam and adjust for lining wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Quick release valve lets air out of the brake chambers quickly when brakes are released. Relay valve applies air quickly to far-away chambers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spring brakes (parking/emergency) in heavy vehicles: strong springs apply the brakes, and air pressure holds them off.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Low air pressure warning (buzzer/light) tells the driver when tank pressure falls below safe level (about 4–5 bar).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air dryer and drain cocks remove moisture from compressed air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air brakes: advantages—large force, unlimited air, no fluid leaks dangerous, trailer brakes easy. Disadvantages—costly, compressor needed, slower response.
recall answer: Large braking force with little effort; easy trailer coupling.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air-over-hydraulic brakes: air pressure works a hydraulic master cylinder (booster) for each circuit. Used in medium trucks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust brake (retarder) closes the exhaust pipe with a valve so the engine slows the vehicle. Electric (eddy current) retarders are also used in buses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake efficiency is tested on a roller brake tester or by a decelerometer. Efficiency = (retardation / g) × 100.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance. Braking distance = v² / (2μg).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Weight transfer during braking loads the front wheels more, so front brakes are made stronger (often discs).
recall answer: Weight shifts to the front under braking.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Proportioning (load-sensing) valve reduces pressure to rear brakes to prevent rear wheel lock-up.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: braking distance
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Brake systems
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Brake systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: A clutch connects and disconnects the engine from the gearbox.
recall answer: Engage and disengage engine power to the gearbox.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Friction clutch principle: two friction surfaces pressed together by springs turn together; separated, they turn freely.
recall answer: Friction between surfaces pressed together transmits torque.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque transmitted by a clutch T = μ W R n (μ friction coefficient, W spring force, R mean radius, n number of friction faces).
recall answer: μ, spring force, mean radius, number of friction surfaces.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Requirements of a clutch: smooth engagement, quick disengagement, enough torque capacity, good heat dissipation, low inertia of driven parts, light pedal.
recall answer: So it stops quickly for easy gear changes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Single plate dry clutch parts: flywheel, clutch (friction) plate, pressure plate, clutch springs, cover, release levers, release (thrust) bearing, clutch shaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch plate is splined to the gearbox input (clutch) shaft, so it can slide but must turn with it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch plate has friction linings on both sides, torsional (damper) springs in the hub and cushion springs (wavy segments) between the linings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: When the pedal is pressed, the release bearing pushes the levers (or diaphragm fingers), pulling the pressure plate back so the clutch plate is free.
recall answer: Pressure plate moves back; clutch disengages.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coil spring clutch uses several coil springs around the pressure plate.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diaphragm clutch uses one dish-shaped steel diaphragm spring instead of coil springs. Its fingers act as release levers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diaphragm clutch advantages: compact, balanced, less pedal effort, pressure does not drop much as lining wears, not affected by centrifugal force.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Multi-plate clutch has several driving and driven plates stacked together.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wet clutch runs in oil; dry clutch runs without oil. Motorcycle multi-plate clutches are usually wet.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cone clutch: friction surfaces are cone-shaped. The wedge action gives high torque for little spring force.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cone clutch drawbacks: tends to stick (grab) and is hard to disengage; used now mostly in synchromesh units.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centrifugal clutch engages automatically as engine speed rises: weights fly out and press the shoes on a drum.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Semi-centrifugal clutch uses both springs and centrifugal weights. Springs carry normal torque; weights add pressure at high speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vacuum clutch uses engine manifold vacuum to operate the clutch through a vacuum cylinder, often triggered by a switch on the gear lever.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydraulic clutch uses a master cylinder at the pedal and a slave cylinder at the clutch to operate the release fork.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electromagnetic clutch: an electromagnet pulls the plates together when current flows.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluid flywheel (fluid coupling): a driving impeller (pump) and a driven turbine (runner) face each other in oil. Oil thrown by the pump drives the turbine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluid coupling cannot multiply torque. Output torque = input torque; there is always some slip (about 2%).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluid flywheel advantages: smooth start, no wear, absorbs shocks, engine does not stall when vehicle stops.
recall answer: Smooth take-up, no wear, shock absorption.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch linings: organic (non-asbestos), ceramic, sintered metal (cerametallic), Kevlar.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch pedal free play: small pedal movement before the release bearing touches the levers (about 20–25 mm).
recall answer: Clutch slip and release bearing wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch slip: engine speed rises but vehicle does not speed up. Causes: worn or oily linings, weak springs, no free play.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch drag: clutch does not fully disengage, so gears grind. Causes: too much free play, warped plate, air in hydraulic clutch.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutch judder (grabbing): jerky take-up. Causes: oily or glazed linings, worn mountings, warped plates.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: Clutches and fluid flywheel
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Clutches and fluid flywheel; standard diploma textbook

key text: A gearbox (transmission) changes the torque and speed from the engine to suit the road, and gives reverse and neutral.
recall answer: Vary torque and speed, give reverse and neutral.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Resistances to vehicle motion: rolling resistance, air resistance, gradient resistance.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Air resistance increases with the square of speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Low gear: high torque, low speed. High gear: low torque, high speed. Top gear is often direct (1:1); overdrive is less than 1:1.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gearbox types: sliding mesh, constant mesh, synchromesh, epicyclic, automatic, CVT.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sliding mesh gearbox: gears on the main shaft slide along splines to mesh with gears on the countershaft (lay shaft).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sliding mesh gearboxes use spur gears and need double de-clutching to change gears quietly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gearbox shafts: primary (input/clutch) shaft, lay shaft (countershaft), main (output) shaft, reverse idler shaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Reverse gear uses an idler gear between lay shaft and main shaft to reverse direction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant mesh gearbox: all gears are always in mesh. Main shaft gears spin freely; dog clutches lock the selected gear to the shaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant mesh gearboxes are quieter and allow helical gears, but still need double de-clutching.
recall answer: Quieter, helical gears, less tooth damage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Synchromesh gearbox: like constant mesh, but has synchronisers (cone clutches) that match gear speeds before the dog teeth engage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Synchroniser types: constant load (pin type) and inertia lock (baulk ring type). Baulk ring is common.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Synchromesh is used in all modern manual cars. Reverse gear is often not synchronised.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Progressive gearbox: gears must be changed in order (1-2-3-4), one after another, as in motorcycles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Selective gearbox: any gear can be selected directly from neutral (H-pattern in cars).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Epicyclic gearbox: uses planetary gear sets (sun, planets, carrier, annulus). Holding one member with a brake band or clutch gives different ratios.
recall answer: By holding one member (sun, carrier or annulus) with brakes/clutches.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a planetary set: hold annulus, drive sun → reduction (low gear). Lock any two members → direct drive. Hold carrier → reverse.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque converter: like a fluid coupling with a third member, the stator (reactor), which multiplies torque (up to about 2–2.5 times) at low speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque converter members: impeller (pump, connected to engine), turbine (connected to gearbox), stator (on a one-way clutch).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coupling point: speed at which the turbine almost matches the impeller and the stator starts to freewheel. Converter then acts as a fluid coupling.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lock-up clutch in modern torque converters mechanically joins impeller and turbine at cruising speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fluid coupling vs torque converter: coupling has 2 members and no torque multiplication; converter has 3 members (with stator) and multiplies torque.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Automatic transmission (AT): torque converter + epicyclic gear sets + hydraulic/electronic controls that shift gears without driver action.
recall answer: Torque converter, planetary gear sets, hydraulic/electronic control.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Automatic selector positions: P (park — locks output), R (reverse), N (neutral), D (drive), L/2 (low).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Engine can be started only in P or N in automatics (neutral safety switch).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: AMT (automated manual transmission): a normal manual gearbox where an ECU and actuators work the clutch and gear shifts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: DCT (dual clutch transmission): two clutches, one for odd and one for even gears, giving very fast shifts.
recall answer: One for odd gears, one for even gears, for fast shifts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: CVT (continuously variable transmission): gives endless ratios between limits using two variable-width pulleys and a belt or chain.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: In a scooter CVT, centrifugal rollers push the drive pulley halves together as speed rises, making the belt ride higher and the ratio taller.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two-wheeler transmissions: primary drive (engine to clutch, by gears or chain), gearbox (constant mesh, sequential), final drive (chain, belt or shaft).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Chain drive: cheap, efficient (about 98%), but needs lubrication and tension adjustment. Belt drive: quiet and clean. Shaft drive: little maintenance, heavier.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gear selector mechanism: gear lever moves selector rods (rails), which move selector forks that slide synchro sleeves or gears.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Interlock mechanism prevents two gears from being engaged at the same time.
