source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Detent (locating) mechanism: spring-loaded balls in notches hold the selector rod in each gear position.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Jumping out of gear causes: worn detents, worn dog teeth or synchro, weak springs, misaligned engine mounts.
recall answer: Worn detent spring/ball or worn dog teeth.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transfer case (4WD vehicles) splits power between front and rear axles and often gives a low range.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: overall gear ratio
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Gearboxes, torque converter, CVT and automatics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Propeller shaft carries power from the gearbox to the rear axle (differential) in front-engine rear-drive vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Propeller shaft is a hollow steel tube, balanced to avoid vibration. Long shafts are made in two parts with a centre bearing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Slip joint (sliding spline joint) lets the propeller shaft change length as the rear axle moves up and down.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Universal joint (Hooke's joint) allows the shaft to drive at an angle that keeps changing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hooke's joint parts: two yokes and a cross (spider) with needle roller bearings.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: A single Hooke's joint at an angle does not give constant speed: the output speeds up and slows down twice per turn.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Using two Hooke's joints with yokes in the same plane and equal angles cancels the speed variation.
recall answer: Two joints in phase with equal angles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other universal joints: flexible (rubber) joint, cross-type, ring-type.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constant velocity (CV) joint gives the same output speed as input at any angle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: CV joint types: Rzeppa (ball type, outer wheel end), tripod (inner, plunging), Bendix-Weiss, Tracta, double Cardan.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: CV joints are covered by rubber boots filled with grease. A torn boot lets dirt in and the joint fails (clicking on turns).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hotchkiss drive: the leaf springs carry the driving thrust and torque reaction from the axle to the frame. Uses an open propeller shaft with two UJs and a slip joint.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque tube drive: the propeller shaft runs inside a rigid tube fixed to the axle. The tube takes torque reaction and drive thrust. Needs only one UJ and no slip joint.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque tube drive allows coil springs, since springs need not carry thrust.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Torque reaction: when the propeller shaft drives the crown wheel, the axle casing tends to turn the opposite way.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driving thrust: force from the driving wheels that pushes the vehicle forward, passed to the frame by springs or radius rods.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Front wheel drive (FWD): engine, gearbox and differential in one unit (transaxle) driving front wheels through CV-jointed drive shafts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: FWD advantages: more space, flat floor, good traction (engine weight on driving wheels), cheaper. Disadvantages: torque steer, heavier steering, more wear on front tyres.
recall answer: More space / good traction / lower cost.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Final drive: crown wheel and pinion give a fixed speed reduction (about 3.5:1 to 6:1) and turn the drive by 90°.
recall answer: Fixed speed reduction and turn drive through 90°.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Differential lets the outer wheel turn faster than the inner wheel on a turn, while driving both.
recall answer: Let driving wheels turn at different speeds on turns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Differential parts: pinion, crown wheel, differential cage (case), two sun (side) gears, two or four planet (star) pinions on a spider.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: On straight roads, planet pinions do not rotate on their own pins; the whole cage turns as one unit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sum of the two wheel speeds = 2 × crown wheel (cage) speed. If one wheel stops, the other turns at twice cage speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Drawback of a normal differential: if one wheel is on mud or ice, it spins and the other gets almost no torque.
recall answer: Loses traction if one wheel slips.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Limited slip differential (LSD) and differential lock reduce or stop wheel spin so the gripping wheel gets torque.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rear axle types by support: semi-floating, three-quarter floating, fully floating.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Semi-floating axle: the half-shaft carries driving torque, bending and vehicle weight; bearing is between shaft and casing. Used in cars.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fully floating axle: the half-shaft carries only driving torque; wheel hub runs on two bearings on the axle casing. Used in trucks and buses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Three-quarter floating: one bearing between hub and casing; shaft carries torque and side loads but not weight.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Axle casing types: banjo type (one-piece with central bulge) and split (carrier) type.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tandem axle: two rear axles close together on heavy trucks to share load. Lift axles can be raised when empty.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Propeller shaft, joints, differential and rear axles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheel types: spoked (wire) wheel, pressed steel disc wheel, light alloy cast wheel, composite wheel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spoked wheel: hub joined to rim by tensioned wire spokes. Light and strong; used on bicycles and some motorcycles. Needs tubes.
recall answer: Spoke holes in the rim leak air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pressed steel disc wheel: rim and disc pressed from steel and welded. Cheap, strong; used on most budget cars and trucks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alloy cast wheel (aluminium or magnesium alloy): light, good looking, better heat removal from brakes, reduces unsprung weight.
recall answer: Light, better cooling of brakes, looks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Composite wheel: made of materials like carbon fibre or a steel rim with alloy centre.
recall answer: Wheel made of combined materials like carbon fibre or steel/alloy.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rim types: drop centre (well base) rim for cars, flat base/divided rims for heavy vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tyre jobs: carry the vehicle weight, grip the road for driving, braking and steering, and absorb small road shocks.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tyre parts: tread, shoulder, sidewall, carcass (plies), bead (with steel wire), breaker/belt, inner liner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tread is the part touching the road; its pattern clears water and gives grip. Sidewall carries markings and flexes.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cross-ply (bias ply) tyre: cords run diagonally (about 30–40°) bead to bead, crossing each other in layers.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radial ply tyre: carcass cords run at 90° across from bead to bead, with steel or textile belts under the tread.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Radial tyres: better grip, longer life, less rolling resistance (better fuel economy), cooler running. Cross-ply: cheaper, stronger sidewalls, harsher ride.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Belted bias tyre: cross-ply carcass with belts under the tread. Between cross-ply and radial.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never mix radial and cross-ply tyres on the same axle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tubeless tyre: no inner tube; an airtight inner liner and tight bead seal hold air on a sealed rim with a valve fixed to the rim.
recall answer: Inner liner and bead seal against the rim.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tubeless advantages: slow air loss on puncture, cooler running, lighter, easy repair. Drawback: needs an airtight rim.
recall answer: Slow loss of air on puncture (no sudden burst).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tread patterns: rib (grooves around the tyre — steering wheels, good on highways), lug (cross bars — driving wheels, traction), rib-lug (mixed), block (off-road/snow), directional, asymmetric.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Minimum tread depth: 1.6 mm (tread wear indicators show this).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aquaplaning: tyre rides on a film of water and loses contact with the road.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Under-inflation: both shoulders wear, tyre heats up, more fuel used, heavy steering, risk of burst.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Over-inflation: centre of tread wears, less grip, hard ride, more damage from impacts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Check tyre pressure when cold, as given on the door label or manual.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Nitrogen inflation: leaks more slowly and has no moisture, so pressure stays steadier.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Factors affecting tyre life and performance: inflation pressure, load, speed, wheel alignment, wheel balance, road surface, driving habits, temperature, brakes.
recall answer: Pressure, load, speed, alignment, balance, road, driving.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheel balancing: weights added to the rim so the wheel spins without vibration. Static and dynamic balance.
recall answer: Prevent vibration and uneven tyre wear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tyre rotation: moving tyres between positions at set intervals so they wear evenly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Tyre size 195/65 R15 91H: 195 mm width, 65% aspect ratio, R = radial, 15-inch rim, 91 = load index, H = speed rating (210 km/h).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Aspect ratio = section height ÷ section width × 100. Low-profile tyres have low aspect ratio.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: DOT/date code on the sidewall: last four digits show week and year of manufacture (e.g. 2324 = 23rd week of 2024).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Retreading: putting new tread on a worn tyre casing. Common for trucks and buses. Retreaded tyres are not allowed on front wheels of buses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Standing waves form in an under-inflated tyre at high speed, causing heat build-up and possible blowout.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: TPMS (tyre pressure monitoring system) warns the driver of low tyre pressure. Mandatory in new cars in India (M1 category) from 2022.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wheels and tyres
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Wheels and tyres; standard diploma textbook

key text: The charging system recharges the battery and supplies electricity to all loads when the engine runs.
recall answer: Recharge battery and power loads while running.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Charging system parts: generator (dynamo or alternator), regulator, battery, ammeter or warning lamp, wiring.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamo (DC generator): armature rotates inside a stationary magnetic field; a commutator and brushes collect DC output.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamo parts: yoke (frame), field poles and coils, armature, commutator, carbon brushes, end covers, pulley.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamos give little or no charge at idle and cannot run at high speed. They are heavy for their output.
recall answer: No charging at idle; low output; cannot run fast.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alternator (AC generator): a rotor (field magnet) rotates inside a stationary stator (output windings). Diodes rectify AC to DC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alternator parts: rotor (claw-pole field), stator (3-phase star or delta windings), slip rings and brushes (carry small field current), rectifier (diode pack), regulator, fan, pulley.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alternator uses 6 diodes (3-phase bridge rectifier) to change AC to DC. Diodes also stop battery current flowing back.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alternator advantages over dynamo: charges at idle, lighter, higher output, higher speed, less maintenance, no cut-out needed.
recall answer: Charges at idle, lighter, higher output, less maintenance.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never disconnect the battery while the alternator is running, and never reverse battery polarity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Regulator controls generator output voltage (about 13.8–14.4 V in a 12 V system) by controlling field current.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamo regulator has three units: cut-out (stops battery discharging into dynamo), voltage regulator, current regulator.
recall answer: Prevent battery discharging through the dynamo.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Alternator needs only a voltage regulator. No cut-out (diodes block reverse flow) and no current regulator (stator limits current itself).
recall answer: It limits its own current (stator reactance).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of regulators: electromechanical (vibrating contact), electronic (transistor), integrated circuit (IC) built into the alternator, ECU-controlled.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Charging warning lamp glows with ignition on and engine off, and goes out when the alternator charges. If it stays on while running, charging has failed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lead-acid battery: 12 V has 6 cells of about 2.1 V each. Electrolyte is dilute sulphuric acid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Specific gravity of battery acid: about 1.26–1.28 when fully charged, about 1.12 when discharged. Checked with a hydrometer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Battery capacity is given in ampere-hours (Ah), e.g. 35 Ah.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Battery plates: positive = lead peroxide (PbO₂), negative = spongy lead (Pb). Both change to lead sulphate on discharge.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sulphation: hard lead sulphate forms on plates if a battery stays discharged, reducing capacity.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Topping up a conventional battery is done with distilled water only, not acid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Maintenance-free (MF) batteries use calcium-lead grids, lose very little water and are sealed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Negative earth system: battery negative is connected to the vehicle body. Almost all vehicles use negative earth.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: When removing a battery, disconnect the negative (earth) terminal first; connect it last.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Dynamo, alternator and charging system
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Dynamo, alternator and charging system; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter motor cranks the engine until it can run on its own.
recall answer: Crank the engine to start it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starting system parts: battery, ignition/starter switch, solenoid (relay), starter motor, drive pinion, flywheel ring gear, heavy cables.
recall answer: Battery, switch, solenoid, starter motor, pinion, ring gear.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter motor is a DC series-wound motor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter motor draws a very high current (about 150–400 A for cars, more for trucks).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter motor parts: yoke, field coils, armature, commutator, brushes, end frames, drive mechanism with pinion.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gear ratio between starter pinion and flywheel ring gear is about 10:1 to 20:1.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter drive engages the pinion with the ring gear for cranking and disengages it once the engine starts.
recall answer: To avoid over-speeding the starter motor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter drive types: Bendix (inertia) drive (inboard and outboard), overrunning (roller) clutch drive, axial (sliding armature), pre-engaged drive.
recall answer: Bendix, overrunning clutch, axial (sliding armature), pre-engaged.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bendix drive: pinion sits on a screwed sleeve on the armature shaft. When the motor spins, the pinion's inertia makes it run along the thread into mesh.
recall answer: Inertia of the pinion on a helical sleeve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: When the engine starts, the ring gear spins the pinion faster, screwing it back out of mesh. A drive spring cushions the shock.
recall answer: Engine spins it faster and it screws back.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Inboard Bendix: pinion moves towards the motor to engage. Outboard Bendix: pinion moves away from the motor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overrunning (roller) clutch drive: a one-way roller clutch lets the pinion freewheel if the engine drives it, protecting the armature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pre-engaged starter: a solenoid first pushes the pinion into mesh using a shift lever, then closes the main contacts to spin the motor. Uses an overrunning clutch.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pre-engaged starter is the most common in modern vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Axial (sliding armature) starter: the whole armature slides forward by magnetic force to mesh the pinion. Used in large diesel engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter solenoid has a pull-in winding (moves plunger) and a hold-in winding (keeps it in).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gear reduction starter has a small high-speed motor with internal reduction gears.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Do not crank for more than about 10–15 seconds at a time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter only clicks: low battery, loose terminals, faulty solenoid contacts. Starter spins but engine does not turn: drive/pinion failure.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Starter motor and drives
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Starter motor and drives; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition system produces a high-voltage spark at the spark plug at the right moment to ignite the mixture in a petrol engine.
recall answer: Produce a timed high-voltage spark at the plug.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition types: battery (coil) ignition, magneto ignition, electronic ignition (transistorised, capacitor discharge), computer controlled, distributor-less (DLI).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark plug needs about 10,000–30,000 volts (modern systems up to 40,000 V).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coil ignition circuit: primary circuit (battery, switch, ballast resistor, primary winding, contact breaker, condenser) and secondary circuit (secondary winding, distributor, HT leads, plugs).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition coil is a step-up transformer: primary has few turns of thick wire (about 200–300); secondary has many turns of thin wire (about 20,000).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: High voltage is induced when the primary current is suddenly broken and the magnetic field collapses.
recall answer: When primary current is broken (field collapses).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Contact breaker (CB) points open and close the primary circuit, worked by a cam on the distributor shaft.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: CB point gap is about 0.35–0.45 mm. Points are made of tungsten.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cam angle (dwell angle): number of degrees of distributor cam rotation during which the points stay closed.
recall answer: Cam angle during which CB points remain closed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Larger point gap → smaller dwell angle. Smaller gap → larger dwell.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Condenser (capacitor) is connected across the CB points. It stops arcing at the points and makes the primary current collapse faster.
recall answer: Prevent arcing at points and speed up field collapse.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Faulty condenser: burnt, pitted points and weak spark.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor sends high voltage to each spark plug in firing order, and houses the CB points, cam, condenser and advance mechanisms.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor rotor turns inside the cap and passes HT current to the cap's side terminals, one for each cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor runs at camshaft speed (half crankshaft speed) in four-stroke engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark advance: the spark must come earlier at higher speed, because the burn takes nearly the same time but the piston moves faster.
recall answer: To give time for burning before piston passes TDC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Centrifugal advance: weights in the distributor fly out with speed and turn the cam forward, advancing the spark.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vacuum advance: a diaphragm connected to manifold vacuum turns the CB base plate, advancing the spark at part load (high vacuum).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Too much advance causes knocking and overheating. Too little (retarded) causes power loss, overheating and high fuel use.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition timing is checked with a stroboscopic timing light aimed at marks on the crank pulley.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ballast resistor in the primary circuit reduces coil current at normal running and is bypassed during cranking for a stronger spark.
recall answer: To give full voltage to the coil for a strong spark.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark plug parts: terminal, insulator (ceramic), metal shell with threads, centre electrode, side (ground) electrode, gasket.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark plug gap is usually about 0.6–1.1 mm.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hot plug: long insulator nose, runs hot, used in low-speed, cool engines. Cold plug: short nose, loses heat fast, used in high-speed, high-compression engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark plug reading: light tan/grey = normal; black sooty = rich mixture; oily = oil burning; white blistered = overheating/lean.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Spark plug types: standard, projected nose, resistor type (reduces radio interference), platinum/iridium tip (long life), multi-electrode.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Magneto ignition makes its own current using magnets; no battery is needed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Magneto gives a weak spark at low speed (starting) and a strong spark at high speed. Coil ignition is the opposite: strong at low speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Low tension magneto: produces low voltage; a separate coil steps it up near the plug. High tension magneto: has both windings inside and gives high voltage directly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rotating armature magneto: windings rotate between fixed magnets. Rotating magnet magneto: magnets rotate, windings fixed (more common).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flywheel magneto: magnets are cast in the flywheel. Used in scooters, mopeds and small engines.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electronic ignition replaces CB points with a transistor switch triggered by a sensor (magnetic pick-up, Hall effect or optical).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transistorised coil ignition (TCI): points carry only a tiny trigger current; a transistor switches the coil current. Fully electronic versions use a pulse generator.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Capacitor discharge ignition (CDI): a capacitor is charged to about 400 V and discharged into the coil primary by a thyristor (SCR).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Pulse generators: magnetic (inductive) pick-up — reluctor and coil; Hall-effect sensor — voltage changes when a vane passes; optical — light beam interrupted.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Computer controlled (programmed/mapped) ignition: ECU sets spark timing from sensors (crank position, speed, load/MAP, coolant temperature, knock sensor) using a stored map.
recall answer: ECU timing map using sensor inputs.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Knock sensor (piezoelectric) on the block detects knocking; the ECU retards timing to stop it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Distributor-less ignition (DLI / DIS): no distributor. Separate coils are triggered by the ECU using a crankshaft position sensor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wasted spark DLI: one coil fires two cylinders at once — one on compression (useful) and one on exhaust (wasted).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coil-on-plug (COP / direct ignition): a separate coil sits directly on each spark plug. No HT leads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft position sensor (CKP) tells the ECU crank angle and speed; camshaft position sensor (CMP) tells which cylinder is on compression.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: HT leads (ignition cables) are resistance or suppression cables (carbon core) to reduce radio interference.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Ignition systems
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Ignition systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 came into force on 1 July 1989. It replaced the old Motor Vehicles Act, 1939.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: The MV (Amendment) Act, 2019 brought big changes: much higher fines, Golden Hour care, Good Samaritan protection, a Motor Vehicle Accident Fund and stricter rules on juveniles.
recall answer: MV (Amendment) Act, 2019 (in force mostly from 1 September 2019).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rules under the Act: Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (CMVR) made by the Centre, and Kerala Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 (KMVR) made by the State.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Main chapters of the MV Act: II licensing of drivers, III licensing of conductors, IV registration, V permits (control of transport vehicles), VII construction and equipment, VIII traffic control.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: More chapters: XI insurance against third-party risks, XII Claims Tribunals, XIII offences, penalties and procedure, XIV miscellaneous.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: A driver must carry the driving licence, registration certificate, insurance certificate and PUC certificate. Transport vehicles also need permit and fitness certificate.
recall answer: DL, RC, insurance certificate, PUC certificate.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Documents can now be shown in electronic form through DigiLocker or mParivahan. These are valid like the paper copies.
recall answer: Yes, electronic copies in DigiLocker/mParivahan are valid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Duty after an accident (Section 134): the driver must get medical help for the injured, take them to hospital if possible, and inform police and insurer.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Golden Hour is the first one hour after a serious injury. Treatment in this time gives the best chance of survival. The 2019 amendment defined it.
recall answer: The first 60 minutes after a traumatic injury.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: A Good Samaritan (Section 134A) is a person who helps an accident victim in good faith. They cannot be harassed or held liable.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Conductor licence is covered by Chapter III (Sections 29 to 38). A conductor of a stage carriage must hold a conductor licence.
recall answer: Conductor of a stage carriage (Chapter III).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Duties of a conductor: issue tickets, not allow overloading, help passengers board safely, keep the bus orderly, and not smoke or misbehave.
recall answer: Issue tickets; prevent overcrowding; safe boarding.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Learner's licence test checks knowledge of traffic rules, signs and driver duties. Driving test checks real driving skill (test of competence).
recall answer: Knowledge of traffic rules, signs and duties.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Every motor vehicle must be registered before use in a public place (Section 39). The registering authority issues a Registration Certificate (RC).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: A non-transport vehicle's registration is valid for 15 years from the date of issue. After that it can be renewed for 5 years at a time.
recall answer: 15 years; renewal for 5 years each time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Transport vehicles need a fitness certificate (Section 56). A new transport vehicle gets fitness for 2 years, then it is renewed every year.
recall answer: 2 years, then 1 year at a time.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Road signs are of three types: mandatory (regulatory), cautionary (warning) and informatory.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mandatory signs are mostly circular. Cautionary signs are triangles pointing up with a red border. Informatory signs are rectangles (often blue or green).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Two mandatory signs have special shapes: STOP is an octagon (8 sides, red), and GIVE WAY is an inverted triangle (point down).
recall answer: STOP: octagon. GIVE WAY: inverted triangle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Red-bordered circle = prohibition (do not do). Blue filled circle = compulsory (you must do), like compulsory left turn or compulsory cycle track.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Traffic lights: red means stop, amber means stop if safe (light is about to change), green means go if the way is clear.
recall answer: Stop before the line unless it is unsafe to stop.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Flashing amber: slow down and go with caution. Flashing red: stop fully, then go when safe.
recall answer: Stop completely, then proceed when safe.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Road markings: broken white centre line = you may cross to overtake if safe; solid line = do not cross; double solid yellow = never cross.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Number plate colours: private white with black letters; transport yellow with black; self-drive rental black with yellow; electric vehicles green.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electric vehicle plates: private EV has green plate with white letters; commercial EV has green plate with yellow letters.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: High Security Registration Plates (HSRP) are aluminium plates with chromium hologram, laser-coded number and snap lock. They are compulsory for all vehicles.
recall answer: Tamper-proof aluminium plate with hologram and laser code.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: The BH (Bharat) series number lets a vehicle move between states without re-registration. It is for defence staff, government staff and private firms in four or more states.
recall answer: No re-registration when moving to another state.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kerala MVD is headed by the Transport Commissioner. Field offices are Regional Transport Offices (RTO) and Sub RTOs. MVIs and AMVIs do inspection and enforcement.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Wings of the MVD: administration, licensing and registration, technical (vehicle inspection), enforcement (road checks, Safe Kerala squads), and road safety.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Permits are granted by the State Transport Authority (STA) and Regional Transport Authority (RTA), set up under Section 68.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vehicle categories: L = two and three wheelers, M = passenger vehicles, N = goods vehicles. M1 is a car with up to 8 seats plus driver.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: Kerala's state code on number plates is KL, and KL-01 is Thiruvananthapuram RTO.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: MV Act basics, signs and the MVD
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — MV Act basics, signs and the MVD; standard diploma textbook

key text: The Indian Roads Congress (IRC), set up in 1934, makes the standards for road design in India.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Road classes (Nagpur Road Plan, 1943): National Highways, State Highways, Major District Roads, Other District Roads and Village Roads.
recall answer: NH, SH, MDR, ODR, Village roads.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carriageway is the part of the road that vehicles use. Shoulders are the strips beside it for stopped vehicles and support.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: IRC widths: single lane 3.75 m; two-lane road without raised kerb 7.0 m; with raised kerbs 7.5 m; intermediate lane 5.5 m.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Maximum legal width of a motor vehicle is 2.6 m. Maximum height for normal vehicles is about 3.8 m.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Formation width (roadway) = carriageway + shoulders. Right of way (land width) is the full land taken for the road, including space for future widening.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camber (cross slope) is the slope given across the road, high in the middle and low at the edges.
recall answer: Drain rainwater from the road surface.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camber values: concrete and high-type bituminous 1.7 to 2%; thin bituminous 2 to 2.5%; WBM and gravel 2.5 to 3%; earth roads 3 to 4%.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camber shapes: parabolic (curved), straight line, or straight with a rounded crown. Heavy rain areas need more camber.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Super elevation (banking) means raising the outer edge of the road on a curve.
recall answer: To counter centrifugal force on curves.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: IRC design super elevation: e = V² / (225 R), with V in km/h and R in metres. This assumes 75% of design speed and no friction.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Full equilibrium equation on a curve: e + f = V² / (127 R). IRC takes the side friction f as 0.15.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Maximum super elevation: 7% in plain and rolling terrain, 10% in hill roads (not snow-bound), 7% in snow-bound areas.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: super elevation
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Gradient is the rise or fall of the road along its length. It is written as 1 in N or as a percent.
recall answer: Rate of rise or fall along the road length.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Types of gradient: ruling (normal design limit), limiting (used where ruling is too costly), exceptional (short stretches only) and minimum (for drainage).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Plain terrain: ruling gradient 3.3% (1 in 30), limiting 5% (1 in 20), exceptional 6.7% (1 in 15).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mountainous terrain: ruling gradient 5% (1 in 20), limiting 6% (1 in 16.7), exceptional 7% (1 in 14.3).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Grade compensation reduces the gradient on a curve. It is (30 + R) / R percent, but not more than 75 / R percent.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sight distance is the length of road a driver can see ahead. It must be enough to stop or overtake safely.
recall answer: Length of road visible ahead to the driver.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stopping sight distance (SSD) = lag distance + braking distance. Lag distance = 0.278 V t; braking distance = V² / (254 f).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: IRC uses a reaction time (perception and brake reaction) of 2.5 seconds, and friction f of 0.35 to 0.40 for SSD.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: stopping sight distance
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Overtaking sight distance (OSD) = d1 + d2 + d3: distance while waiting behind, distance during the overtake, and distance the oncoming car moves.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Intermediate sight distance (ISD) = 2 × SSD. For SSD, driver eye height is taken as 1.2 m and object height as 0.15 m.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Extra widening on curves = mechanical widening (n l² / 2R) + psychological widening (V / 9.5√R).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: A transition curve joins a straight road to a circular curve gradually. The ideal shape is the spiral (clothoid).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Intersections are at-grade (roads meet at the same level, such as rotary or channelised junctions) or grade-separated (flyovers and interchanges).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: A four-leg junction of two two-way roads has 32 conflict points: 16 crossing, 8 merging and 8 diverging.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: A rotary (roundabout) makes all traffic go one way around a central island. Vehicles merge and leave by weaving.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cloverleaf, trumpet and diamond are types of grade-separated interchanges. A full cloverleaf removes all crossing conflicts.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: PCU (Passenger Car Unit) compares vehicles to one car. A car is 1 PCU; bigger or slower vehicles have higher PCU values.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Highway engineering basics
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Highway engineering basics; standard diploma textbook

key text: Third-party insurance is compulsory for every motor vehicle in a public place (Section 146). Driving without it is an offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: The three parties: first party is the owner, second party is the insurance company, third party is any other person hurt or whose property is damaged.
recall answer: Any other person (not insurer or insured) who suffers loss.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Policy types: liability only (third party), comprehensive (third party + own damage) and standalone own damage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Third-party property damage cover is limited to ₹7.5 lakh. Third-party death and injury cover has no upper limit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compulsory personal accident cover for the owner-driver is ₹15 lakh.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India) regulates insurers and licenses surveyors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: A motor claim above ₹50,000 must be assessed by a surveyor licensed by IRDAI (Insurance Act, Section 64UM).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Kinds of survey: spot survey (at the accident site), final survey (estimates loss at the garage), re-inspection (checks repairs before payment).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: IDV (Insured Declared Value) is the current market value of the vehicle. It is the most the insurer pays for total loss or theft.
recall answer: Insured Declared Value: maximum sum insured.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: IDV = manufacturer's listed price minus age depreciation: up to 6 months 5%, 6 months–1 year 15%, 1–2 years 20%, 2–3 years 30%, 3–4 years 40%, 4–5 years 50%.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: For vehicles older than 5 years, IDV is fixed by agreement between the insurer and the owner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: IDV
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Depreciation on parts: rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes and batteries 50%; fibreglass parts 30%; glass parts nil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Metal parts depreciation by age: under 6 months nil, 6 months–1 year 5%, 1–2 years 10%, 2–3 years 15%, 3–4 years 25%, 4–5 years 35%, 5–10 years 40%, over 10 years 50%.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Zero depreciation is an add-on cover. With it, the insurer pays the full cost of replaced parts without deducting depreciation.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Constructive total loss (CTL): when repair cost plus salvage handling exceeds 75% of IDV, the vehicle is treated as a total loss.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Salvage is the value of the damaged vehicle or parts left after the loss. It goes to the insurer or is deducted from the claim.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: No Claim Bonus (NCB) is a discount on the own-damage premium for claim-free years: 20%, 25%, 35%, 45%, then 50% after five years.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: NCB belongs to the owner, not the vehicle. It can be moved to a new vehicle. It is lost when a claim is made.
recall answer: No, it stays with the owner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Compulsory deductible (excess) is the fixed amount the owner pays in every own-damage claim, such as ₹1,000 for private cars up to 1,500 cc.
recall answer: Fixed part of each claim borne by the owner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Factors in assessing loss: cause matches the accident story, extent of damage, repair or replace, depreciation, salvage, policy conditions and valid DL and permit.
recall answer: Cause, extent of damage, depreciation, salvage, policy terms.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: A claim can be refused if the driver had no valid licence, was drunk, or the vehicle was used for a purpose not covered, such as hire use under a private policy.
recall answer: No valid DL, drunk driving, or misuse of vehicle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Insurance principles: utmost good faith, insurable interest, indemnity, subrogation, contribution and proximate cause.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Subrogation: after paying the claim, the insurer gets the owner's right to recover money from the person who caused the loss.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Claim steps: tell the insurer quickly, file FIR if needed (theft, injury), survey, approval, repair, re-inspection, payment.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Theft claim needs FIR, all keys, RC, and a non-traceable report from police. It is settled on IDV.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Premium depends on IDV, engine cc, age, zone (city), NCB, add-ons and voluntary deductible. Third-party premium rates are fixed by IRDAI.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Motor insurance and surveying
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Motor insurance and surveying; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electronic fuel injection (EFI) sprays fuel through injectors that an electronic control unit (ECU) controls. It replaced the carburettor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Advantages of EFI: better mileage, lower emissions, easy cold start, more power, smooth running and no carburettor icing.
recall answer: Better economy, lower emissions, easy cold start.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Throttle body injection (TBI) is single-point injection: one or two injectors placed at the throttle body, feeding all cylinders.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: MPFI (multi-point fuel injection) has one injector for each cylinder, spraying into the intake port just before the inlet valve.
recall answer: Into the intake port, just before the inlet valve.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: MPFI injection timing: simultaneous (all at once), group or batch (in groups) and sequential (each injector in firing order).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: GDI (gasoline direct injection) sprays petrol directly into the combustion chamber at high pressure (about 50–200 bar).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel supply in EFI: electric fuel pump in the tank → filter → fuel rail → injectors. A pressure regulator keeps about 3 bar.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: An injector is a solenoid valve. The ECU opens it for a few milliseconds; this time is called pulse width. Longer pulse width gives more fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: The ECU (ECM) is the brain. It reads sensors (inputs), decides, and drives actuators (outputs) like injectors and ignition coils.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Open loop: ECU uses fixed maps without O2 feedback (cold start, full throttle). Closed loop: ECU corrects fuel using the oxygen sensor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Stoichiometric air-fuel ratio for petrol is 14.7:1 by mass. Lambda (λ) = actual AFR ÷ 14.7. λ = 1 is ideal; above 1 lean; below 1 rich.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: lambda
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: MAF sensor (mass air flow) measures air entering the engine. Hot-wire type: incoming air cools a heated wire; more current needed means more air.
recall answer: Air cools a heated wire; current to keep it hot shows air mass.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: MAP sensor (manifold absolute pressure) measures pressure (vacuum) in the intake manifold. ECU uses it with rpm to estimate engine load (speed-density method).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Throttle position sensor (TPS) is a potentiometer on the throttle shaft. It tells the ECU how much the throttle is open.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Coolant temperature sensor is an NTC thermistor: its resistance falls as temperature rises. A cold engine gets a richer mixture.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Intake air temperature (IAT) sensor is also an NTC thermistor. Cold air is denser, so the ECU adds more fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Oxygen (lambda) sensor sits in the exhaust. The zirconia type makes 0.1 to 0.9 V: high voltage (about 0.9 V) means rich, low (about 0.1 V) means lean.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Crankshaft position sensor (CKP) gives engine speed and piston position. If it fails, there is no spark or injection, so the engine will not start.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Camshaft position sensor (CMP) tells which cylinder is on its compression stroke. It is needed for sequential injection.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Knock sensor is a piezoelectric sensor on the block. When it detects knocking, the ECU retards the ignition timing.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hall effect and inductive (magnetic) sensors are used for crank, cam and wheel speed. Inductive sensors make AC voltage; Hall sensors give a digital square wave.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Actuators in EFI: injectors, idle air control valve, ignition coils, fuel pump relay, electronic throttle motor, EGR valve and canister purge valve.
recall answer: Injectors, idle air control valve, ignition coil.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Idle air control (IAC) valve lets a little air bypass the closed throttle to keep idle speed steady when AC or lights are switched on.
recall answer: Control idle speed by bypass air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Drive-by-wire (electronic throttle control): the accelerator pedal has a sensor, and a motor opens the throttle. There is no cable.
recall answer: An electric motor controlled by the ECU.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: If a sensor fails, the ECU uses default values (limp home mode) and lights the MIL (check engine light).
recall answer: Safe reduced running using default values after a fault.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: OBD (on-board diagnostics) stores fault codes (DTCs like P0301). A scan tool reads them through the 16-pin OBD-II connector. OBD-II is compulsory with BS-VI.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: CRDI (common rail direct injection) is the diesel system where a high-pressure pump keeps fuel in a common rail. ECU-controlled injectors spray it into each cylinder.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: CRDI pressure is very high: about 1,350 to 2,000 bar or more. Very fine spray burns cleaner.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: CRDI parts: low-pressure feed pump, high-pressure pump, common rail, rail pressure sensor, pressure control valve, solenoid or piezo injectors, ECU.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: CRDI can inject several times per cycle: pilot (small, before), main, and post injection.
recall answer: To reduce diesel knock and noise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Piezo injectors open faster than solenoid injectors, so they allow more precise and more injections per cycle.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Older diesel systems: inline pump, rotary (distributor) pump and unit injector. In these, pressure rises with engine speed.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: PSC trap: the term 'MPFI' is for petrol engines; 'CRDI' is for diesel engines. Both are electronically controlled injection.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electronic fuel injection, sensors and CRDI; standard diploma textbook

key text: Main pollutants from petrol engines are CO, HC and NOx. Diesel engines give mainly NOx and particulate matter (PM or soot).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Sources of HC in a petrol car without controls: exhaust about 60%, crankcase blow-by about 20%, evaporation from tank and carburettor about 20%.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Carbon monoxide (CO) forms from incomplete burning with a rich mixture. It is colourless, odourless and poisonous; it binds with haemoglobin in blood.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hydrocarbons (HC) are unburnt fuel. They come from rich mixture, misfire, and fuel left near cold cylinder walls (quench layer).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: NOx (oxides of nitrogen) forms at very high combustion temperature with extra oxygen. High compression and slightly lean mixtures increase NOx.
recall answer: High combustion temperature with excess oxygen.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: In diesels there is a NOx–PM trade-off: cooler burning cuts NOx but raises soot, and hotter burning cuts soot but raises NOx.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve sends blow-by gases from the crankcase back into the intake manifold to be burnt.
recall answer: Burn crankcase blow-by gases by sending them to the intake.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: EVAP system: an activated charcoal canister stores fuel vapour from the tank. When the engine runs, the purge valve sends the vapour to the intake to burn.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: EGR (exhaust gas recirculation) sends a small part of exhaust gas (about 5–15%) back into the intake.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: EGR is closed at idle and at full throttle. It works at part load and cruising.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: A three-way catalytic converter changes CO to CO₂, HC to CO₂ and water, and NOx to nitrogen, all at once.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Catalysts used: platinum and palladium for oxidation (CO, HC); rhodium for reduction of NOx.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Catalytic converter body is a ceramic honeycomb (cordierite) or metal monolith with an alumina washcoat holding the precious metals.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: A catalytic converter starts working above about 250–300 °C (light-off temperature). It needs λ close to 1.
recall answer: Temperature at which the catalyst starts working (about 250–300 °C).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Leaded petrol poisons the catalytic converter. Misfire overheats and melts it. Leaded petrol was banned in India from 2000.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: A two-way (oxidation) catalyst controls only CO and HC. Diesels use a diesel oxidation catalyst (DOC).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Afterburner (thermal reactor) burns leftover CO and HC in the hot exhaust manifold with extra air supplied by air injection.
recall answer: Burns remaining CO and HC in the exhaust with added air.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel particulate filter (DPF) traps soot. It cleans itself by burning the soot (regeneration) at high temperature.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: SCR (selective catalytic reduction) sprays urea solution (AdBlue or DEF, 32.5% urea) into the exhaust. It forms ammonia, which turns NOx into nitrogen and water.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel smoke colours: black = incomplete burning (overload, faulty injector, rich); blue = lube oil burning; white = unburnt fuel at cold start or water in fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel smoke is measured with a smoke meter. Hartridge type measures light absorption (opacity); Bosch type uses filter paper blackening.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Diesel PUC test is a free acceleration smoke test. Result is the light absorption coefficient k in m⁻¹.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Exhaust gas analysers use NDIR (non-dispersive infrared) to measure CO, CO₂ and HC in petrol vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Lab methods: FID (flame ionisation detector) for HC and chemiluminescence for NOx.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: PUC limits for BS-IV and later petrol 4-wheelers: idle CO 0.3% and HC 200 ppm; at high idle CO 0.2% and λ 1 ± 0.03.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Bharat Stage (BS) norms are India's emission standards, based on European (Euro) norms. They are set by the central government under CMVR.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Timeline: BS-I (India 2000) in 2000, BS-IV across India from April 2017, BS-V skipped, BS-VI across India from 1 April 2020.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook
