key text: BS-VI fuel has only 10 ppm sulphur, against 50 ppm in BS-IV fuel.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: BS-VI Phase 2 (April 2023) added Real Driving Emission (RDE) tests and on-board monitoring of emissions.
recall answer: Real Driving Emission (RDE) testing and on-board monitoring.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificate shows that the vehicle passed the emission test. Driving without a valid PUC is an offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Noise is measured with a sound level meter in dB(A). Pressure horns and multi-tone horns are banned; changing the silencer to make noise is an offence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cleaner fuels: CNG and LPG give less CO and PM. Ethanol blending (E20, 20% ethanol in petrol) cuts imports and emissions.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: How a three-way catalytic converter cleans exhaust
recall answer: So oxidation of CO/HC and reduction of NOx both happen.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vehicle pollution and its control
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Vehicle pollution and its control; standard diploma textbook

key text: Active safety systems help avoid a crash (ABS, ESC, traction control). Passive safety systems protect people during a crash (seat belt, airbag, crumple zone).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: ABS (anti-lock braking system) stops the wheels from locking during hard braking, so the driver can still steer.
recall answer: Keeps steering control by preventing wheel lock.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: ABS parts: wheel speed sensors, ABS ECU, and the hydraulic modulator (valves and a pump). The modulator releases and reapplies pressure many times a second.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: With ABS the brake pedal pulses during hard braking. The driver should keep pressing firmly, not pump the pedal.
recall answer: Press firmly and hold; do not pump.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: ABS is compulsory for two-wheelers above 125 cc, and CBS (combined braking system) for two-wheelers up to 125 cc, from April 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: EBD (electronic brake force distribution) shares braking force between front and rear wheels according to load. It works with ABS.
recall answer: Distributes brake force to each wheel by load.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Traction control stops the drive wheels from spinning when accelerating. It cuts engine torque or brakes the spinning wheel, using ABS wheel sensors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: ESC (electronic stability control, also ESP) stops skids. Using steering angle, yaw rate and lateral acceleration sensors, it brakes single wheels to keep the car on its path.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: A three-point seat belt holds the chest and hips. Its inertia reel locks when the car slows suddenly.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Seat belt pretensioner pulls the belt tight at the start of a crash, often with a small explosive charge. Load limiter then lets out a little belt to reduce chest injury.
recall answer: Tightens the belt instantly in a crash.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Airbags are SRS (supplementary restraint system). They work along with the seat belt, not instead of it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Airbag working: crash sensor (accelerometer) → airbag ECU → igniter → gas generator fills the bag in about 30 milliseconds.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Older airbags used sodium azide to make nitrogen gas. A clock spring (spiral cable) connects the steering wheel airbag while the wheel turns.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Driver airbag is compulsory in cars from July 2019. Front passenger airbag is compulsory for new cars from 2021.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Never fit a rear-facing child seat in front of an active passenger airbag. Children should sit in the rear seat.
recall answer: Front seat with an active airbag.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Since July 2019 new cars must have: driver airbag, seat belt reminder, speed alert, rear parking sensors and a manual override for central locking.
recall answer: Driver airbag, seat belt reminder, speed alert, parking sensors.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Speed alert system: beeps once above 80 km/h, beeps often above 100 km/h, and beeps continuously above 120 km/h.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Parking sensors are ultrasonic sensors in the bumper. The beep gets faster as an object gets closer. A reverse camera shows the area behind.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cruise control keeps a set speed without pressing the accelerator. Adaptive cruise control uses radar to keep a safe gap to the car ahead.
recall answer: Keeps a safe distance using radar.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Cruise control turns off when the driver presses the brake or clutch.
recall answer: Press brake (or clutch) or the cancel switch.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Power windows, power seats and power mirrors use small DC motors. Power seats may have memory positions; power windows may have anti-pinch.
recall answer: A small DC motor and regulator.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Rain-sensing wiper: an infrared light beam is reflected inside the windscreen. Raindrops change the reflection, and the wipers start and adjust speed.
recall answer: Change in infrared light reflection by water on glass.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Automatic climate control keeps a set cabin temperature using cabin, outside and sun-load sensors. It controls blower speed, blend door and compressor.
recall answer: Cabin temperature, ambient or sun-load sensor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Car AC cycle: compressor → condenser (gives out heat) → receiver-drier → expansion valve → evaporator (absorbs cabin heat) → compressor.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Car AC refrigerant is R-134a; newer cars use R-1234yf, which harms the climate much less.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Noise control: sound insulation and damping sheets, rubber engine mounts, good silencers, sealed doors and active noise cancellation.
recall answer: Insulation, rubber mounts, silencer, active noise cancellation.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Remote keyless entry (RKE) locks and unlocks doors by a radio signal from the key fob. Smart keys (passive entry) unlock when the key is near.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: An immobiliser has a transponder chip in the key. The engine ECU allows starting only if the chip's code matches.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: GPS finds position using signals from satellites. At least 4 satellites are needed for a 3D position. India's own system is NavIC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Vehicle location tracking devices (VLTD) with emergency buttons are compulsory in public service vehicles (AIS-140) from 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Speed governors (speed limiting devices) are needed in transport vehicles: usually 80 km/h; 60 km/h for dumpers and tankers; 40 km/h for school buses.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: TPMS (tyre pressure monitoring system) warns when a tyre's pressure is low.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: ADAS (advanced driver assistance systems) includes automatic emergency braking (AEB), lane keep assist, blind spot warning and adaptive cruise.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: Comfort and safety systems
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Comfort and safety systems; standard diploma textbook

key text: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) runs only on a battery and electric motor. Main parts: battery, motor, controller (inverter), charger and BMS.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: EV benefits: zero tailpipe emission, low running cost, fewer moving parts, quiet running, full torque from zero speed and regenerative braking.
recall answer: No tailpipe emission, low running cost.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: EV challenges: high purchase cost, range anxiety, long charging time, few chargers, battery cost and disposal, and load on the power grid.
recall answer: Fear that the battery will run out before reaching a charger.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Most EVs use lithium-ion batteries. Common types are NMC (nickel manganese cobalt) and LFP (lithium iron phosphate).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: LFP batteries are safer and last more cycles but store less energy per kg. NMC stores more energy but costs more and is less heat-stable.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Battery capacity is measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). More kWh means more range.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: EV range
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Worked example: charging time
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: BMS (battery management system) watches each cell's voltage and temperature, finds the state of charge (SOC), balances cells and protects against overcharge and overheating.
recall answer: State of charge (how full the battery is).
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Thermal runaway is when a lithium cell overheats, which makes it hotter still, leading to fire. Cooling systems and BMS prevent it.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: AIS-156 sets battery safety tests for L-category (two and three wheeler) EVs. It was tightened in 2022–23 after e-scooter fires.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: EV motors: BLDC (brushless DC) in scooters, PMSM (permanent magnet synchronous motor) in most cars, and induction motors in some cars.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: A hub motor sits inside the wheel hub and drives the wheel directly. It is common in electric scooters.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: The inverter changes battery DC into AC for the motor and controls its speed. A DC-DC converter lowers high voltage to 12 V for lights and accessories.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: EVs usually have a single-speed reduction gear and no clutch or multi-speed gearbox.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Regenerative braking uses the motor as a generator while slowing down. It charges the battery and reduces brake wear.
recall answer: Motor acts as generator during braking to charge the battery.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: AC charging uses the car's on-board charger to change AC to DC. DC fast charging sends DC directly to the battery, bypassing the on-board charger.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Common charging standards in India: CCS2 for DC fast charging of cars, Type 2 for AC; older Bharat AC-001 and DC-001 standards; CHAdeMO in a few vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: EV high-voltage cables are orange. Before repair, the high-voltage system must be isolated using the service disconnect and insulated tools.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: A hybrid electric vehicle (HEV) has both an IC engine and an electric motor with a battery.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Series hybrid: the engine only drives a generator; the motor alone drives the wheels. A range-extender EV is a series hybrid.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Parallel hybrid: both the engine and the motor can drive the wheels, alone or together.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Series-parallel (power split) hybrid uses a planetary gear set to mix engine and motor power. Toyota's hybrid system is an example.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Mild hybrid: a small motor (often 48 V starter-generator) helps the engine but cannot drive the car alone. Strong (full) hybrid can drive short distances on electricity only.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Plug-in hybrid (PHEV) has a bigger battery that can be charged from the grid. It drives some distance on electricity, then uses the engine.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Hybrid parts: IC engine, motor-generator, battery pack, power control unit (inverter), and power split device or transmission.
recall answer: Engine, motor-generator, battery, power control unit.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) makes electricity from hydrogen and oxygen in a fuel cell. The only exhaust is water.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: FAME India scheme (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Hybrid and Electric Vehicles) gave subsidies: FAME I from 2015, FAME II from 2019 (₹10,000 crore).
recall answer: Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: PM E-DRIVE scheme (2024) replaced FAME II to support e-two-wheelers, e-three-wheelers, e-buses and charging stations.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Other EV support: GST on EVs 5% (petrol cars up to 28%), no registration fee for battery vehicles, permit exemption for battery-operated transport vehicles, and green plates.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP) 2020 was launched in 2013. Kerala brought its own EV policy in 2019.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Low-speed e-scooters with top speed up to 25 km/h and motor up to 250 W are not 'motor vehicles' under CMVR. They need no registration or licence.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: E-rickshaw and e-cart were added by the 2015 amendment (Section 2A). Top speed is up to 25 km/h; an e-rickshaw carries up to 4 passengers and 40 kg luggage.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Old petrol or diesel vehicles can be converted to EV or hybrid with approved retrofit kits (AIS-123), and the change is entered in the RC.
recall answer: Yes, with an approved retrofit kit, endorsed in the RC.
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook

key text: Electric and hybrid vehicles
source: Kerala PSC AMVI syllabus, Cat. No. 517/2022 — Electric and hybrid vehicles; standard diploma textbook
